20.s: Mediterranean climate receives most of its rainfall during winter because
o: the subtropical high-pressure belt dominates in winter
cold ocean currents produce continuous monsoon rainfall
westerly depressions and cyclonic systems affect the region in winter
the trade winds reverse and produce convection throughout winter
20.x: In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.
20.tq: Connect the seasonal pressure-belt shift with the timing of rainfall.

20.s: Which one of the following climatic descriptions is characteristic of the Mediterranean climate?
o: Severe winters and short, cool summers
Hot, wet summers and long, dry winters
Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters
Rainfall throughout the year with negligible annual range
20.x: Mediterranean climate is characterised by hot, dry and sunny summers and mild, wet winters.
20.tq: Separate Mediterranean conditions from savanna and taiga descriptions.

20.s: Mediterranean climate is generally found between approximately
20.x: Mediterranean climate occurs mainly between 30° and 45° north and south, particularly on the western margins of continents.
20.tq: Recall both the latitude belt and the western-margin setting.

20.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with Mediterranean climate?
20.x: Darwin is not among the listed Mediterranean climatic locations. Mediterranean conditions occur in places such as Santiago, Cape Town and Perth.
20.tq: Find the location outside the recognised Mediterranean-climate regions.

20.s: In India, the climatic type corresponding to Koeppen’s As classification is associated with the
20.x: Koeppen’s As climate, characterised by dry summers and winter rainfall, occurs on the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu.
20.tq: Match the Koeppen symbol with its Indian regional occurrence.

20.s: The Mediterranean climatic region is popularly known for the cultivation of
20.x: Mediterranean regions are known as orchard lands and are associated with citrus fruits, grapes and wine production.
20.tq: Use the characteristic crop association to identify the climate.

20.s: A region has a very small annual temperature range of 2–3°C and receives rainfall in every month. Which climate does it most likely represent?
20.x: A very small annual temperature range and year-round rainfall are characteristic of the equatorial climate.
20.tq: Identify the climate from its strongest temperature-range and rainfall clues.
20.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

20.s: A region experiences a hot, wet summer followed by a long dry winter. This description most closely corresponds to
20.x: Hot wet summers and long dry winters are characteristic of savanna or monsoon climatic conditions.
20.tq: Distinguish summer-rain climates from the winter-rain Mediterranean type.
20.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

20.s: A climate with very high temperatures, a very large daily range and annual rainfall below 25 cm is characteristic of
20.x: Extreme heat, a large diurnal temperature range and rainfall below 25 cm indicate a hot desert climate.
20.tq: Combine rainfall amount with daily temperature range to identify the desert type.
20.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

20.s: Which climatic description correctly represents the taiga climate of Siberia?
o: Warm dry summer and mild wet winter
Long severe winter, short cool summer and very large annual range
Warmest month below 10°C with no seasonal contrast
Very small annual temperature range and rainfall every month
20.x: The taiga climate has a long severe winter, a short cool summer and a very large annual temperature range.
20.tq: Select the description containing the decisive seasonal-range features of taiga.
20.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

20.s: A place where the warmest month has a temperature below 10°C is generally classified as having
20.x: A warmest-month temperature below 10°C is a defining descriptive feature of the tundra climate.
20.tq: Use the temperature threshold as the decisive classification clue.
20.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

20.s: Who proposed the empirical climatic classification scheme based on mean temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation?
20.x: Wladimir Koeppen proposed an empirical climatic classification based on mean temperature and precipitation, with climate types linked to natural vegetation.
20.tq: Use the direct name-and-contribution recall method.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ‘A’ group in Koeppen’s classification?
o: Polar climate with the warmest month below 10°C
Dry climate in which evaporation exceeds precipitation
Cold snow-forest climate with the coldest month below -3°C
Tropical humid climate with the coolest month above 18°C
20.x: The A group represents tropical humid climates where the coolest month has a temperature above 18°C.
20.tq: Match the group with its defining temperature criterion.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the major groups of Koeppen’s classification:
1. Group B represents dry climates in which evaporation exceeds precipitation.
2. Group C represents warm temperate climates with the coldest month between -3°C and 18°C.
3. Group D represents cold snow-forest climates with the coldest month below -3°C.
4. Group E represents polar climates with the warmest month below 10°C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: All four statements correctly state the criteria for Koeppen groups B, C, D and E.
20.tq: Check each numerical boundary before selecting the coded combination.

20.s: In Koeppen’s classification, the letter ‘H’ denotes:
20.x: H denotes a highland climate in which low temperatures are controlled mainly by altitude.
20.tq: Discriminate the exact classification letter from similar-sounding alternatives.

20.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the second letters used in Koeppen’s classification?
20.x: The second letter f indicates that there is no dry season. The letters m, w and s indicate monsoon, dry winter and dry summer respectively.
20.tq: Use the confusable-pair method for the letters w and s.

20.s: The code ‘BWhw’ in the Indian application of Koeppen’s classification represents which region?
o: West Rajasthan and parts of Punjab
The Ganga plain and northern Madhya Pradesh
20.x: BWhw is associated with extreme western Rajasthan. BShw covers western Rajasthan, north-west Gujarat and parts of Punjab.
20.tq: Separate the closely related BShw and BWhw regional codes.

20.s: Which one of the following climatic codes is associated with Arunachal Pradesh?
20.x: Arunachal Pradesh is represented by the Dfc climatic code in the given Indian application of Koeppen’s scheme.
20.tq: Link the regional location directly with its classification code.

20.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Amw — West coast south of Goa
2. As — Coromandel coast and Tamil Nadu
3. Aw — Most of the peninsular plateau
4. Dfc — Arunachal Pradesh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
20.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the Indian regional applications of Koeppen’s classification.
20.tq: Verify each code-region pair independently before choosing the complete combination.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Thornthwaite’s classification from Koeppen’s classification?
o: Thornthwaite used only natural vegetation, whereas Koeppen used only altitude.
Thornthwaite emphasised precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, whereas Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation.
Thornthwaite was based exclusively on pressure, whereas Koeppen was based on winds.
Both classifications used exactly the same criteria and symbols.
20.x: Thornthwaite’s scheme is based on precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, including potential evapotranspiration. Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation.
20.tq: Identify the reversed-criteria trap in a comparison question.

20.s: Thornthwaite first proposed his climatic classification in 1931 and revised it in:
20.x: Thornthwaite proposed the classification in 1931 and revised it in 1948.
20.tq: Use the date-pair recall method and distinguish the revision year from the original year.

20.s: In Thornthwaite’s classification, potential evapotranspiration is used as an indicator of:
20.x: Thornthwaite’s classification considers precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, with potential evapotranspiration serving as the basis for thermal efficiency.
20.tq: Connect the technical term with the exact classification basis.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its climatic criterion in the classification table?
20.x: Group D has the coldest month below -3°C, not above 18°C. The criteria stated for Groups A, B and E are correct.
20.tq: Find the one reversed temperature criterion.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT an element of climate listed in climatological analysis?
20.x: The listed elements of climate are temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, precipitation and cloudiness. Lithology is not an element of climate in this list.
20.tq: Identify the outsider from the standard set of climatic elements.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s: Weather is best defined as:
o: The state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time
The long-term distribution of vegetation over a region
The average atmospheric condition over a period of 30 years
The seasonal variation in ocean currents only
20.x: Weather refers to the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time. Climate refers to average weather over a long period.
20.tq: Distinguish the short-term weather definition from the long-term climate definition.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s: The World Meteorological Organization’s standard period for describing climate normals is:
20.x: The WMO standard describes climate using average weather conditions over a period of 30 years.
20.tq: Test the standard numerical period directly.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A climograph represents monthly temperature and rainfall of a station on one chart.
2. Temperature is generally represented by a line in a climograph.
3. Rainfall is generally represented by bars in a climograph.
4. A climograph can assist in identifying the climate type of a place.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: A climograph combines monthly temperature, shown by a line, and rainfall, shown by bars, and is used to interpret the climate type of a station.
20.tq: Combine the chart components and their use before selecting the coded answer.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s: The current IMD rainfall normal for the southwest monsoon season, based on the 1971–2020 period, is:
20.x: The IMD normal rainfall for June–September, based on the 1971–2020 base period, is 868.6 mm.
20.tq: Separate the precise normal value from nearby numerical distractors.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s: The IMD rainfall normal of 868.6 mm refers to rainfall during:
20.x: The 868.6 mm normal is the long-period average rainfall for the June–September southwest monsoon season.
20.tq: Match the numerical normal with its exact reference period.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s: The current IMD rainfall normal of 868.6 mm is calculated using which base period?
20.x: The current IMD normal uses the 1971–2020 base period.
20.tq: Discriminate the correct climatological base period from standard alternatives.
20.sec: Elements of climate, weather vs climate, climograph

20.s: Magnetic minerals preserved in the sediments of Bakhira Lake are significant because they provide a record of Indian monsoon variability extending approximately:
20.x: Magnetic minerals in Bakhira Lake sediments provide an approximately 25,000-year record of Indian monsoon variability.
20.tq: Use the distinctive large-number recall technique.

20.s: Bakhira Lake, associated with the palaeoclimatic record of Indian monsoon variability, is located in:
20.x: Bakhira Lake is in Uttar Pradesh, and its sediments preserve the long-term monsoon record.
20.tq: Match the named geographical feature with its state.

20.s: Which of the following statements about projected coastal climatic conditions is correct?
o: About 40 coastal districts may warm by over 1°C by 2040, with Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu receiving excess southwest-monsoon rain.
About 15 coastal districts may cool by over 1°C by 2040, with Andhra Pradesh receiving deficient monsoon rain.
All coastal districts are projected to warm by exactly 1°C by 2040.
Only inland districts of Andhra Pradesh are projected to experience excess southwest-monsoon rain.
20.x: The projection concerns about 40 coastal districts warming by more than 1°C by 2040, while Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are expected to receive excess southwest-monsoon rain.
20.tq: Reject extreme words such as ‘all’ and ‘exactly’ while retaining the precise projection.

20.s: Which statement correctly describes the geographical and climatic setting of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It lies between 19°07′ N and 25°41′ N and is classified as E/ET.
It lies between 8°41′ N and 15°07′ N and is classified as Amw.
It lies entirely north of 20° N and is classified as BWhw.
It lies between 12°41′ N and 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, or tropical wet and dry climate.
20.x: Andhra Pradesh extends from 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, representing a tropical wet and dry climate.
20.tq: Combine latitude limits with the correct Koeppen code and reject reversed ranges.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four climatic regions identified in Andhra Pradesh?
20.x: The four regions are humid coastal, deltaic, semi-arid Rayalaseema and hill micro-climates. Ladakh is not an Andhra Pradesh climatic region.
20.tq: Find the geographically misplaced regional description.

20.s: Which one of the following groups consists only of hill micro-climate locations in Andhra Pradesh?
20.x: Araku, Lambasingi and Horsley Hills are cited as examples of hill micro-climates in Andhra Pradesh.
20.tq: Select the option containing the complete location group without an outside place.

20.s: According to the recent classification stated for Andhra Pradesh, the State has:
20.x: The recent APSES 2024–25 classification identifies six agro-climatic zones in Andhra Pradesh. Older books may state seven.
20.tq: Handle the current-versus-older figure distinction carefully.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the number of agro-climatic zones in Andhra Pradesh and India?
o: Andhra Pradesh has fifteen, while India has six.
Andhra Pradesh has four, while India has fifteen.
Andhra Pradesh has six, while India has fifteen.
Both Andhra Pradesh and India have seven.
20.x: The current figures stated are six agro-climatic zones for Andhra Pradesh and fifteen for India.
20.tq: Use the direction of comparison to avoid interchanging state and national figures.

20.s: The recent listing of Andhra Pradesh’s six agro-climatic zones is arranged with reference to:
o: The four major climatic regions of the world
20.x: The APSES 2024–25 table lists the six agro-climatic zones against the 13 pre-2022 districts.
20.tq: Identify the administrative framework attached to the classification.

20.s: Which statement regarding the year 2025 and La Niña is correct?
o: 2025 was the first year without any ocean warming.
2025 had no association with La Niña conditions.
2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record.
2025 was the coldest La Niña year on record.
20.x: The stated current-affairs fact is that 2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record.
20.tq: Reject absolute reversals of the reported climate record.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the global ocean climate in 2025:
1. Oceans held more than 90% of the excess heat.
2. Approximately 90% of the ocean surface experienced marine heatwaves.
3. Less than 10% of the excess heat was held by the oceans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the oceans held more than 90%, not less than 10%, of the excess heat.
20.tq: Spot the numerical reversal in the false statement.

21.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in 1988 by which of the following organisations?
21.x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
21.tq: Use the institutional-founder trap by identifying the correct pair of establishing organisations.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s:
With reference to the IPCC, consider the following statements:
1. It has 195 members.
2. It conducts original climate research as its principal activity.
3. It assesses the existing scientific literature on climate change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: The IPCC has 195 members and assesses available scientific literature. It does not conduct research of its own as its principal activity.
21.tq: Separate the assessment function from the research function before selecting the coded combination.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s: The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the IPCC in 2007 was shared with which of the following persons?
21.x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.
21.tq: Test the person-organisation association directly, using nearby climate personalities as distractors.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (IPCC Working Group)
A. Working Group I
B. Working Group II
C. Working Group III

List-II (Subject)
1. Mitigation
2. Physical science basis
3. Impacts, adaptation and vulnerability

A B C
(a) 2 3 1
(b) 3 1 2
(c) 1 2 3
(d) 2 1 3
21.x: Working Group I deals with the physical science basis, Working Group II with impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and Working Group III with mitigation.
21.tq: Start from the sure pair: Working Group I is associated with the physical science basis.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s: The Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR1.5) was published in which year?
21.x: The IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C was published in 2018.
21.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall method for a named assessment report.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s: According to the SR1.5 pathway, limiting global warming to 1.5°C requires global carbon dioxide emissions to fall approximately by what percentage from 2010 levels by 2030?
21.x: The SR1.5 assessment indicated that global CO₂ emissions need to decline by about 45% from 2010 levels by 2030.
21.tq: Test the exact percentage through a close-range numerical comparison.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s: In the context of climate policy, 'net zero' means that:
o: All greenhouse-gas emissions are stopped permanently.
Natural emissions are completely eliminated from the atmosphere.
Human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through sinks or capture.
Only carbon dioxide emissions are reduced to zero without removals.
21.x: Net zero is achieved when human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through natural sinks or technological capture, resulting in zero net addition.
21.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish net emissions from gross emissions.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) Synthesis Report:
1. It was released on 20 March 2023.
2. Warming during 2011–2020 had already reached about 1.1°C.
3. It indicated that 1.5°C warming is likely to be breached in the early 2030s.
4. It stated that emissions may peak after 2035 without affecting the mid-century net-zero objective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. AR6 indicated that emissions must peak before 2025; therefore statement 4 is incorrect.
21.tq: Find the single time-related reversal in the final statement.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the projected timeline of the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report cycle?
o: Working Group reports by about mid-2028 and the Synthesis Report by late 2029
Working Group reports by late 2025 and the Synthesis Report by mid-2026
Working Group reports by mid-2030 and the Synthesis Report by late 2031
Working Group reports by late 2029 and the Synthesis Report by mid-2032
21.x: The AR7 cycle began in July 2023, with Working Group reports expected around mid-2028 and the Synthesis Report by late 2029.
21.tq: Use the first-and-last timeline points to identify the correct sequence.
21.sec: IPCC assessment reports, thresholds, net zero, SR1.5  [APPSC]

21.s: Which of the following greenhouse gases has a global warming potential of 1 and serves as the reference gas for 100-year GWP calculations?
21.x: Carbon dioxide is assigned a 100-year GWP of 1 and is used as the reference gas.
21.tq: Test the reference-value association rather than the gas with the highest GWP.

21.s: Which one of the following greenhouse gases is correctly matched with its approximate 100-year global warming potential?
21.x: Methane has an approximate 100-year GWP of 28–36. Nitrous oxide is about 265–298, CFCs/HFCs range from 1,000 to 23,000, and SF₆ is about 23,900.
21.tq: Compare the gas-value pairs and reject swapped GWP ranges.

21.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Methane — Rice paddies, livestock and waste dumps
2. Nitrous oxide — Fertilisers, industry and combustion
3. CFCs/HFCs — Coolants and foams
4. Sulphur hexafluoride — Dielectric fluid in switchgear
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
21.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the principal sources listed for these greenhouse gases.
21.tq: Check each source against the gas before using the all-inclusive option.

21.s: Which one of the following greenhouse gases is synthetic only and has a 100-year GWP range of approximately 1,000–23,000?
21.x: CFCs and HFCs are synthetic gases with 100-year GWP values ranging approximately from 1,000 to 23,000.
21.tq: Discriminate between natural, mixed-origin and synthetic greenhouse gases using both origin and GWP.

21.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the approximate atmospheric lifetime given for it?
21.x: Water vapour has an approximate atmospheric lifetime of nine days. Methane lasts about 12 years, nitrous oxide about 114 years, and carbon dioxide has a much wider lifetime range of about 100–1,000 years.
21.tq: Use the lifetime column to catch swapped values between similar greenhouse gases.

21.s: Perfluoromethane is associated principally with which industrial activity?
21.x: Perfluoromethane is released in association with aluminium production.
21.tq: Test the pollutant-industry association directly.

21.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas.
2. Human beings increase atmospheric water vapour mainly indirectly by warming the air.
3. Water vapour is primarily a synthetic greenhouse gas released by refrigeration equipment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas, and human influence on it is mainly indirect through warming. It is natural, not primarily synthetic or refrigeration-derived.
21.tq: Use the natural-versus-synthetic distinction to reject the false statement.

21.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 2024 atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration is correct?
o: It was about 423.9 ppm, the highest level in approximately two million years.
It was close to the pre-industrial level and represented a two-century low.
It was below 280 ppm because of increased ocean absorption.
It was about 1,000 ppm, the highest level since the formation of Earth.
21.x: CO₂ reached about 423.9 ppm in 2024, described as the highest concentration in approximately two million years; the pre-industrial level was around 280 ppm.
21.tq: Combine a precise numerical value with its historical comparison.

21.s: Which of the following correctly represents the recent global temperature ranking?
o: 2019 was the hottest year globally, while 2000–2010 comprise the eleven warmest years.
2024 was the hottest year on record, while 2015–2025 comprise the eleven warmest years.
2025 was the hottest year on record and 2024 was the second warmest.
Only the years after 2020 entered the list of the eleven warmest years.
21.x: 2024 was the hottest year on record, and the period 2015–2025 contains the eleven warmest years in the record.
21.tq: Check the ranking and the complete year range rather than accepting a partly familiar claim.
21.sec: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice  [APPSC]

21.s:
With reference to global temperature records, consider the following statements:
1. The temperature in 2024 was about 1.55°C above the pre-industrial level.
2. The temperature in 2025 was approximately 1.43°C above the pre-industrial level.
3. 2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All three statements are correct: 2024 was about 1.55°C above the pre-industrial level, 2025 about 1.43°C, and 2025 was the warmest La Niña year recorded.
21.tq: Verify each numerical and ranking statement before selecting the complete combination.
21.sec: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice  [APPSC]

21.s: Which of the following correctly compares warming in India with warming over global land areas?
o: India has warmed about 1.59°C since 1900, compared with about 0.7°C for global land.
India has experienced cooling since 1900, while global land has warmed about 0.7°C.
India has warmed about 0.7°C since 1900, compared with about 1.59°C for global land.
Both India and global land have warmed exactly 2°C since 1900.
21.x: India has warmed approximately 0.7°C since 1900, whereas global land areas have warmed about 1.59°C.
21.tq: Watch for reversal of the two values in a comparison question.
21.sec: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice  [APPSC]

21.s: Which year was recorded as India’s warmest year since 1901?
21.x: The year 2024 was recorded as India’s warmest year since 1901.
21.tq: Distinguish the national record year from the separate seventh-warmest year.
21.sec: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice  [APPSC]

21.s: The Gangotri Glacier has retreated by approximately how much since 1935?
21.x: Gangotri Glacier has retreated approximately 1,700 metres since 1935, with global warming identified as the cause of its melting.
21.tq: Use the exact distance and reference year together to avoid range-based guessing.
21.sec: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice  [APPSC]

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent indicators of climate change:
1. Global sea level has risen by about 11 cm since 1993.
2. Arctic sea ice is near record-low levels.
3. Antarctic sea ice was at its third-lowest level.
4. Earth’s energy imbalance was at a 65-year peak.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All four statements describe the reported indicators: sea-level rise of about 11 cm, near-record-low Arctic sea ice, third-lowest Antarctic sea ice and a 65-year peak in energy imbalance.
21.tq: Treat each indicator as an independent evidence point before selecting the combined answer.
21.sec: Evidence - warmest years, glaciers, sea level, sea ice  [APPSC]

21.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the short-lived climate pollutants listed?
21.x: The listed short-lived climate pollutants are black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone. Water vapour is not included in that list.
21.tq: Find the odd item outside the specified pollutant group.

21.s: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition is associated with action against:
21.x: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition works to address short-lived climate pollutants such as black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.
21.tq: Match the coalition with the precise environmental problem it addresses.

21.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the source and lifetime of black carbon?
o: Incomplete combustion of diesel, biomass and coal — days to weeks
Rice paddies and livestock — about 12 years
NOx and VOCs in sunlight — weeks to months
21.x: Black carbon is produced by incomplete combustion of diesel, biomass and coal and remains in the atmosphere for days to weeks.
21.tq: Separate the source-lifetime pair of black carbon from those of methane, ozone and synthetic gases.

21.s: Black carbon deposited on snow accelerates glacier melting primarily because it:
o: Reduces snow albedo and increases absorption of solar energy
21.x: Black carbon darkens snow, reduces its albedo and increases the absorption of solar energy, thereby accelerating glacier melt.
21.tq: Apply the albedo concept to the snow-and-black-carbon situation.

21.s: Tropospheric ozone is formed mainly from which combination in sunlight?
o: Nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds
21.x: Tropospheric ozone is formed through reactions involving nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in sunlight.
21.tq: Test the precursor-pollutant relationship rather than the lifetime of the pollutant.

21.s:
Which of the following is a direct physical cause of sea-level rise associated with climate change?
1. Thermal expansion of seawater
2. Melting of ice
3. Increased snow albedo
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
21.x: Sea-level rise results from thermal expansion of seawater and melting of ice. Increased snow albedo would reflect more radiation and is not a cause of sea-level rise.
21.tq: Identify the two established mechanisms and reject the reversed albedo effect.

21.s: Which pair of South Pacific islets was reported to have been submerged in 1999?
21.x: The uninhabited South Pacific islets Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea were reported to have been submerged in 1999. Kiribati and Tuvalu are countries at risk from sea-level rise.
21.tq: Distinguish submerged islets from countries identified as being at risk.

21.s: Which one of the following statements about climate-related coral bleaching is correct?
o: Large-scale warm-water reef collapse begins only above 3°C, and reefs recover within two years.
Reefs recover immediately once the atmospheric temperature falls for one season.
The approximately 1.2°C threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse has already been crossed, and reefs need more than 15 years to recover.
Coral reefs are unaffected by warming below 4°C.
21.x: The approximately 1.2°C threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse has already been crossed, and coral reefs require more than 15 years to recover.
21.tq: Combine the threshold and recovery-period figures while rejecting exaggerated alternatives.

21.s: If global warming exceeds approximately 2°C, which ecological change has been projected for parts of the Amazon?
o: Complete conversion of the Amazon into tundra
Elimination of all grassland from the region
Conversion of parts of the Amazon into savanna
Permanent expansion of tropical glaciers across the Amazon
21.x: Beyond approximately 2°C of warming, parts of the Amazon may undergo a shift towards savanna conditions.
21.tq: Apply the temperature threshold to the projected ecosystem transformation.

21.s: Which one of the following statements regarding ocean and mountain ecosystem impacts is correct?
o: Ocean acidity has increased by about 30% since the Industrial Revolution, and up to 25% of mountain species may face extinction.
Ocean acidity has fallen by 30% since the Industrial Revolution, while no mountain species face extinction risk.
Ocean acidity has remained unchanged, while exactly 50% of mountain species face extinction.
Ocean acidity has increased by 3%, and mountain species are unaffected because of altitude.
21.x: Ocean acidity has increased by about 30% since the Industrial Revolution, and AR6 estimates that up to 25% of mountain species may face extinction.
21.tq: Watch for reversed trends and altered percentages in the paired-impact statement.

21.s: According to the reported 2025 assessment for India, extreme weather events resulted in approximately:
o: 441 deaths and damage to 1.74 million hectares of crops
17.4 million deaths and damage to 4,419 hectares of crops
44,190 deaths and damage to 174 million hectares of crops
4,419 deaths and damage to 17.4 million hectares of crops
21.x: The reported 2025 impacts in India included 4,419 deaths and damage to approximately 17.4 million hectares of crops.
21.tq: Keep the count and area units attached to the correct quantities.

21.s: Warmer and wetter conditions can widen the geographical range of which category of diseases?
o: Only genetic disorders such as haemophilia
Only deficiency diseases such as scurvy
Non-infectious diseases exclusively caused by ageing
Vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue
21.x: Warmer and wetter conditions can expand the range of vectors and thereby increase the spread of diseases such as malaria and dengue.
21.tq: Link the environmental change to the disease category and examples it affects.

21.s: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 projects that continuation of current policies would result in global warming of approximately:
21.x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 estimates approximately 2.8°C of warming under current policies.
21.tq: Use the distinctive report-specific figure rather than the familiar 1.5°C or 2°C targets.
21.sec: Climate science recognition and major reports  [APPSC]

21.s: With full implementation of nationally determined contributions (NDCs), the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 places projected global warming in which range?
21.x: Full implementation of current NDCs is associated with projected warming of about 2.3–2.5°C.
21.tq: Distinguish the NDC projection from the higher current-policy projection.
21.sec: Climate science recognition and major reports  [APPSC]

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025:
1. Emissions must fall by 35% from 2019 levels by 2035 to limit warming to 2°C.
2. Emissions must fall by 55% from 2019 levels by 2035 to limit warming to 1.5°C.
3. An overshoot of 1.5°C is described as very likely during this decade.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All three statements are correct: the stated reductions are 35% for the 2°C pathway and 55% for the 1.5°C pathway, while a 1.5°C overshoot is considered very likely this decade.
21.tq: Check each numerical statement separately before selecting the coded combination.
21.sec: Climate science recognition and major reports  [APPSC]

21.s: The WMO publication titled State of the Global Climate 2025 was released on:
21.x: The report was released on World Meteorological Day, 23 March 2026.
21.tq: Link the named international report with its stated release occasion and date.
21.sec: Climate science recognition and major reports  [APPSC]

21.s: Which phrase was associated with the climate indicators in the WMO State of the Global Climate 2025 report?
21.x: The report described the climate indicators as “flashing red.”
21.tq: Test the exact official expression rather than a general paraphrase.
21.sec: Climate science recognition and major reports  [APPSC]

21.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Precession — wobble of the rotational axis
21.x: Precession refers to the wobble of Earth’s axis. Eccentricity concerns orbital shape and obliquity concerns axial tilt.
21.tq: Separate the three easily confusable components of the Milankovitch cycles.

21.s: Milankovitch cycles are associated primarily with changes in:
o: Earth’s magnetic field and ocean salinity
Volcanic activity, continental drift and solar flares
Atmospheric pressure, humidity and cloud cover
Orbital eccentricity, axial obliquity and precession
21.x: Milankovitch cycles comprise changes in eccentricity, obliquity and precession, which help drive ice-age cycles.
21.tq: Identify the complete three-part set instead of choosing a related but different natural factor.

21.s: The Little Ice Age is generally placed approximately between:
21.x: The Little Ice Age is placed approximately in the period 1500–1850.
21.tq: Use the historical range as the discriminator among overlapping climate periods.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about solar output and recent global warming:
1. Satellite observations since 1978 show no net increase in solar output.
2. Recent warming can therefore not be explained by an increasing solar output.
3. Satellite observations establish that solar output has continuously declined since 1978.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The evidence indicates no net increase, not a continuous decline, in solar output since 1978.
21.tq: Reject the stronger but unsupported word ‘continuously’ in the third statement.

21.s:
Which of the following natural factors are identified as possible influences on climate?
1. Volcanic activity
2. Continental drift
3. Ocean currents
4. Fertiliser use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
21.x: Volcanic activity, continental drift and ocean currents are natural climate influences. Fertiliser use is an anthropogenic cause associated with nitrous oxide emissions.
21.tq: Classify each factor as natural or human-induced before using the code.

21.s: Volcanic eruptions can produce a short-term cooling effect mainly because:
o: Volcanic gases permanently remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Sulphur dioxide and ash form aerosols that reflect sunlight
Volcanic dust increases the absorption of solar radiation by the surface
Lava directly lowers ocean temperatures worldwide
21.x: Sulphur dioxide and ash generate cooling aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.
21.tq: Connect the natural event with its atmospheric mechanism and radiative effect.

21.s: Stratospheric aerosol injection is proposed as a form of geoengineering because it seeks to:
o: Increase the absorption of sunlight by the stratosphere
Reflect sunlight by forming sulphuric-acid aerosols
Increase the concentration of greenhouse gases in the upper atmosphere
Remove all water vapour from the troposphere
21.x: In this proposal, sulphur dioxide forms sulphuric-acid aerosols that reflect sunlight, imitating the cooling effect of volcanic eruptions.
21.tq: Identify the intended physical process rather than the name of the intervention alone.

21.s: In the context of stratospheric aerosol injection, the term ‘termination shock’ refers to:
o: Rapid warming if aerosol injection is abruptly stopped
The destruction of the ozone layer by volcanic ash alone
A sudden cooling caused by stopping fossil fuel use
The permanent cessation of solar radiation
21.x: Termination shock denotes rapid warming that could occur if the cooling intervention were stopped suddenly.
21.tq: Discriminate between the proposed intervention and the risk created by terminating it.

21.s: Cirrus cloud thinning is intended to cool the Earth by:
o: Seeding high cirrus clouds so that more outgoing heat escapes
Spraying sea salt into low marine clouds
Making high cirrus clouds thicker so that they reflect more sunlight
Increasing the amount of sulphur dioxide in volcanic plumes
21.x: Cirrus cloud thinning seeks to reduce the insulating effect of high cirrus clouds and allow more outgoing heat to escape.
21.tq: Match the geoengineering proposal with the direction of its radiative effect.

21.s: Marine cloud brightening involves the use of sea-salt spray primarily to:
o: Absorb infrared radiation in the stratosphere
Suppress all forms of cloud formation
Reduce the salinity of the surface ocean
Act as cloud condensation nuclei and brighten clouds
21.x: Sea-salt spray can act as cloud condensation nuclei, potentially making marine clouds brighter.
21.tq: Identify the material used and its immediate atmospheric function.

21.s: A study associated with marine cloud brightening suggested that it could weaken:
21.x: The cited study suggested that marine cloud brightening could weaken a Super El Nino.
21.tq: Use the specific claimed climate-system effect to distinguish the proposal from other interventions.

21.s: Which one of the following is the largest contributor to anthropogenic climate change among the causes listed?
o: Fossil fuel burning involving coal, oil and gas
21.x: Burning coal, oil and gas is identified as the largest contributor among the listed anthropogenic causes.
21.tq: Separate the dominant human source from natural climate drivers.

21.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deforestation and land-use change can remove carbon sinks.
2. Agricultural fertilisers contribute to nitrous oxide emissions.
3. Livestock contribute to methane emissions.
4. Deforestation increases carbon sinks in all circumstances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Deforestation and land-use change generally remove or reduce carbon sinks rather than increase them in all circumstances.
21.tq: Find the absolute and reversed statement before selecting the coded option.

21.s: Which of the following correctly describes the contrasting climate effects of the aerosol types listed below?
o: All aerosols invariably cool the air
Black and brown carbon cool the air, while sulphate droplets warm it
All aerosols invariably warm the air
Black and brown carbon warm the air, while sulphate droplets cool it
21.x: Black and brown carbon have a warming effect on the air, whereas sulphate droplets exert a cooling effect.
21.tq: Test the reversed comparison between warming and cooling aerosol types.

21.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sulphate droplets — warming of the air
21.x: Sulphate droplets are associated with cooling, not warming, of the air. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
21.tq: Find the single reversed cause-effect pair in a set of close environmental associations.

21.s: COP31 is scheduled to meet in which country and month?
21.x: COP31 is scheduled to meet in Türkiye in November 2026.
21.tq: Combine the host location and month to avoid confusing the event with another climate meeting.

21.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the CMIP7 scenarios mentioned in current climate assessments?
o: They place the world below 1°C by 2100 under current policies.
They exclude all scenarios involving human emissions and project no warming.
They retain SSP5-8.5 as the only scenario and project 1.5°C by 2100.
They drop the worst-case SSP5-8.5 scenario and place the world near 2.8°C by 2100.
21.x: The CMIP7 scenarios drop the worst-case SSP5-8.5 pathway and place projected warming near 2.8°C by 2100.
21.tq: Test both parts of a current-affairs statement: the scenario change and the projected temperature.

21.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with climate-related concerns in Andhra Pradesh?
21.x: Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are identified in connection with heatwaves. Uppada in the Kakinada region is associated with coastal erosion.
21.tq: Match each environmental hazard with its geographical locations before comparing the options.

21.s: Uppada, in the Kakinada region, is particularly associated with which climate-related impact?
21.x: Coastal erosion at Uppada near Kakinada is identified as an Andhra Pradesh climate-related concern.
21.tq: Use the location-specific impact rather than a general climate-change effect.

21.s: APSES 2024–25 tracks climate action under which Sustainable Development Goal?
21.x: APSES 2024–25 tracks climate action under SDG 13.
21.tq: Recall the exact SDG number associated with climate action.

22.s: Which one of the following best describes the continental shelf?
o: A flat deep-sea surface covered mainly by red clay
An apron of sediment at the foot of the continental slope
A gently sloping, shallow submerged prolongation of the continent
A steep-sided depression at a plate boundary
22.x: The continental shelf is the gently sloping, shallow submerged edge or prolongation of a continent.
22.tq: Use the precise definition of the landform rather than confusing adjacent relief features.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: The continental shelf generally extends up to approximately which depth?
22.x: The continental shelf generally extends to about 200 metres depth.
22.tq: Distinguish the characteristic depth range of the shelf from those of deeper ocean-floor zones.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the continental shelf:
1. It contains some of the richest fishing grounds.
2. It is an important zone for oil and natural gas resources.
3. It is the deepest and steepest part of the ocean floor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: The continental shelf is important for fisheries, oil and gas. It is not the deepest and steepest part of the ocean floor; that description relates to oceanic deeps and trenches.
22.tq: Find the statement that reverses the comparison between the shallow shelf and the deepest relief.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: Which one of the following features is particularly associated with the continental slope?
o: The highest concentration of usable fresh water
The shallowest extension of the continent
22.x: The continental slope is a steep descent from the shelf edge and is associated with submarine canyons and trenches.
22.tq: Match the characteristic feature with the correct ocean-floor division.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s:
Arrange the following ocean-floor divisions in descending order of their usual depth:
A. Continental shelf
B. Continental slope
C. Deep-sea plain
D. Oceanic deeps
Select the correct sequence.
22.x: Oceanic deeps are deepest, followed by deep-sea plains, continental slopes and continental shelves.
22.tq: Apply the depth sequence from the continental margin towards the deepest oceanic relief.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: The continental rise is best described as:
o: A narrow trench formed at a convergent plate boundary
A shallow platform extending from the coast to 200 metres
A zone of floating pelagic organisms
An apron of sediment at the foot of the continental slope
22.x: The continental rise is an apron of accumulated sediment at the foot of the continental slope and forms a transition towards the deep plain.
22.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring continental-margin features by location and form.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: Which one of the following statements about the deep-sea or abyssal plain is correct?
o: It is generally confined to the first 200 metres below sea level.
It forms the flattest and smoothest extensive surface on the Earth's surface.
It is the steepest section between the shelf and the continental rise.
It consists exclusively of active volcanoes and earthquake zones.
22.x: The deep-sea plain, generally about 3,000–6,000 metres deep, is the flattest and smoothest extensive surface on Earth and is the most extensive part of the ocean floor.
22.tq: Reject extreme words such as ‘exclusively’ and identify the defining comparison.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: Polymetallic nodules are particularly associated with which part of the ocean floor?
22.x: Polymetallic nodules occur on the deep-sea plains.
22.tq: Link a resource to its characteristic ocean-floor environment.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s:
With reference to oceanic deeps and trenches, consider the following statements:
1. They are generally long, narrow and steep-sided.
2. They are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
3. They occur mostly in the Pacific Ocean.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Oceanic deeps or trenches are long, narrow and steep-sided, commonly occur at plate-convergence zones, and are associated with volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Most are located in the Pacific Ocean.
22.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only when each characteristic belongs to the same relief feature.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: The deep sea below about 200 metres is described as the:
22.x: The deep sea below 200 metres is described as the oldest and largest biome, occupying about 90–95 per cent of Earth's habitable space.
22.tq: Pair the numerical extent with the correct superlative description.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: About what proportion of Earth's habitable space is occupied by the deep sea below 200 metres?
22.x: The deep sea below 200 metres accounts for approximately 90–95 per cent of Earth's habitable space.
22.tq: Test a distinctive quantitative range directly and avoid confusing it with the share of Earth's surface covered by oceans.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: One fathom is equal to:
22.x: A fathom is a unit of depth equal to 6 feet, or approximately 1.83 metres.
22.tq: Distinguish the exact unit conversion from nearby length values.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: Which one of the following correctly explains echo sounding or sonar as a method of determining ocean depth?
o: Depth is calculated by dividing the speed of sound by the full round-trip time.
Depth is obtained by multiplying the speed of sound in water by half the round-trip time of the echo.
Depth is calculated from the salinity and temperature of surface water alone.
Depth is measured by observing the colour of the sea surface.
22.x: Echo sounding measures the time taken by a sound pulse to travel to the sea floor and return; depth equals speed multiplied by half the round-trip time.
22.tq: Apply the physical principle and identify why the return journey is divided by two.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: Isobaths are lines joining places having equal:
22.x: Isobaths join points of equal depth, especially on maps of submerged relief.
22.tq: Separate depth contours from lines representing equal pressure, temperature or salinity.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: A hypsometric curve represents the:
o: Share of Earth's surface occurring at different land heights and sea depths
Variation of salinity with distance from the coast
Distribution of marine deposits according to grain size
Variation of ocean currents with latitude
22.x: A hypsometric curve shows the proportion of Earth's surface at different elevations on land and depths in the sea.
22.tq: Identify the graph by its complete subject coverage—both land heights and sea depths.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s:
Consider the following statements about CTD instruments:
1. They measure conductivity, which is related to salinity.
2. They measure temperature.
3. They measure depth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: CTD instruments measure conductivity, temperature and depth; conductivity is used to determine salinity.
22.tq: Check all three components of the standard CTD abbreviation and instrument function.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: In 2026, CTD sensors were fitted to sharks for the purpose of:
o: Measuring the thickness of continental shelves
Determining the age of red clay deposits
22.x: The sensors fitted to sharks were used to collect ocean data relevant to hurricane forecasting.
22.tq: Connect an instrument’s field deployment with its stated practical application.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Neritic zone — open-ocean water column beyond the shelf
Pelagic zone — high-water mark to about 200 metres over the shelf
Mesopelagic zone — approximately 200 to 1,000 metres depth
Benthic zone — only the surface layer of the open ocean
22.x: The mesopelagic or twilight zone extends from about 200 to 1,000 metres. The neritic zone overlies the shelf, the pelagic zone is beyond the shelf, and the benthic zone is the sea floor.
22.tq: Use direct pair elimination by checking each zone against its depth or location.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: The mesopelagic zone is also known as the:
22.x: The mesopelagic zone, extending approximately from 200 to 1,000 metres, is commonly called the twilight zone.
22.tq: Discriminate between closely related marine-zone names and their standard synonym.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: Which one of the following is associated with the mesopelagic zone?
22.x: Lanternfishes and deep-sea shrimps are characteristic organisms of the mesopelagic zone, which also contributes to the biological carbon pump.
22.tq: Identify the organisms associated with the correct ecological zone.
22.sec: Depth mapping methods and units

22.s: Terrigenous deposits are best described as deposits that:
o: Are formed exclusively from the shells of microscopic marine organisms
Occur only in the deepest trenches and contain no land-derived material
Consist only of volcanic dust transported through the atmosphere
Originate from land and accumulate mainly on continental shelves and slopes
22.x: Terrigenous deposits are derived from land and are deposited mainly on continental shelves and slopes.
22.tq: Distinguish land-derived deposits from pelagic biological and inorganic deposits.
22.sec: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

22.s:
Consider the following statements about terrigenous deposits:
1. They may include gravel, sand, silt and mud.
2. Their coarseness generally decreases away from the shore.
3. They become coarser as the distance from the shore increases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Terrigenous material may consist of gravel, sand, silt and mud. Coarser material is deposited near the coast, while finer material settles farther offshore; therefore statement 3 is false.
22.tq: Spot the reversed trend in a comparison statement about distance from the coast.
22.sec: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

22.s: Which one of the following is NOT a pelagic deposit?
22.x: Calcareous ooze, siliceous ooze and red clay are pelagic deposits. Coastal gravel is a land-derived terrigenous deposit.
22.tq: Find the exception by separating deep-sea deposits from coarse coastal material.
22.sec: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

22.s: Calcareous ooze is primarily composed of:
o: Fine inorganic clay and volcanic dust alone
Gravel and sand transported from continental rivers
Silica skeletons of diatoms and radiolarians
Lime shells of tiny organisms such as globigerina and pteropods
22.x: Calcareous ooze consists mainly of the lime shells of tiny organisms, including globigerina and pteropods.
22.tq: Match each ooze type with its distinctive biological composition.
22.sec: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

22.s: Siliceous ooze is associated with the remains of:
22.x: Siliceous ooze is formed from the silica skeletons of organisms such as diatoms and radiolarians and is common in colder or deeper waters.
22.tq: Use the composition-based distinction between calcareous and siliceous ooze.
22.sec: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

22.s: Which one of the following statements about red clay is correct?
o: It is restricted to river mouths and estuaries.
It is the most widespread deep-sea deposit and is largest in the deep Pacific.
It is formed exclusively from lime shells in warm shallow seas.
It occurs only on continental shelves and consists mainly of gravel.
22.x: Red clay consists of fine inorganic clay and volcanic dust. It is the most widespread deep-sea deposit and is particularly extensive in the deep Pacific.
22.tq: Use the superlative and location together to identify the correct deposit.
22.sec: Ocean deposits - terrigenous vs pelagic

22.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Ocean-floor feature)
a. Continental shelf
b. Continental slope
c. Deep-sea plain
d. Oceanic deeps

List-II (Characteristic)
i. Active volcanoes and strong earthquakes
ii. Canyons and trenches
iii. Rich fishing grounds and oil and gas
aiv. Flattest and smoothest extensive surface

Codes:
22.x: The continental shelf is rich in fisheries and hydrocarbons; the slope has canyons and trenches; the deep-sea plain is the flattest surface; and oceanic deeps are associated with volcanoes and earthquakes.
22.tq: Start from the sure pair—shelf with fishing grounds and oil—and eliminate incompatible codes.
22.sec: Ocean bottom relief → characteristic feature

22.s: Which is the correct order of the oceans from largest to smallest by area?
22.x: The order by area is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic; the Arctic Ocean is the smallest.
22.tq: Recall the complete size ranking and use the smallest ocean as a final check.
22.sec: Oceans - size ranking, share of surface under water

22.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Oceans cover approximately 70–71 per cent of Earth's surface.
2. Oceans contain approximately 97 per cent of Earth's water.
3. Oceans constitute the largest part of the hydrosphere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Oceans cover about 70–71 per cent of Earth's surface, contain about 97 per cent of its water, and form the largest component of the hydrosphere.
22.tq: Verify whether all quantitative and comparative statements refer consistently to oceans.
22.sec: Oceans - size ranking, share of surface under water

22.s: Approximately what percentage of Earth's water is contained in the oceans?
22.x: Approximately 97 per cent of Earth's water is contained in the oceans.
22.tq: Separate the share of Earth's water from the share of Earth's surface covered by oceans.
22.sec: Oceans - size ranking, share of surface under water

22.s: According to the stated broad division of Earth's water, approximately what proportions are represented by ice and usable fresh water, respectively?
o: About 1 per cent and about 2 per cent
About 70 per cent and about 27 per cent
About 2 per cent and about 1 per cent
About 97 per cent and about 2 per cent
22.x: About 2 per cent of Earth's water is represented as ice and about 1 per cent as usable fresh water in the stated broad division.
22.tq: Keep the small percentages distinct from the approximately 97 per cent oceanic share.
22.sec: Oceans - size ranking, share of surface under water

22.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the distribution of fresh water among its major stores?
o: Lakes and rivers together far exceed groundwater.
Groundwater far exceeds the water stored in lakes and rivers.
Groundwater, lakes and rivers contain equal amounts of fresh water.
Rivers contain nearly all usable fresh water, whereas groundwater is negligible.
22.x: Groundwater far exceeds the amount of fresh water stored in lakes and rivers.
22.tq: Identify the correct comparative relationship rather than choosing an absolute claim.
22.sec: Oceans - size ranking, share of surface under water

22.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a seamount?
o: A deep valley cut across a continental shelf
A flat-topped island formed by wave erosion
A ring-shaped coral reef surrounding a lagoon
A submarine volcanic mountain that does not reach the ocean surface
22.x: A seamount is an undersea volcanic mountain whose summit does not reach the ocean surface.
22.tq: Use the precise-definition approach to distinguish closely related submarine landforms.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding guyots:
1. A guyot is a flat-topped seamount.
2. Its top is planed by waves before the feature sinks below the sea surface.
3. It is a ring-shaped coral reef around a central lagoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A ring-shaped coral reef around a central lagoon is an atoll, not a guyot.
22.tq: Separate the correct statements from a swapped definition of an atoll.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s: An atoll is best described as a:
o: Ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef enclosing a central lagoon
Deep gorge cut across the continental slope
Flat-topped submarine mountain formed only by tectonic uplift
Submarine volcanic peak with a pointed summit
22.x: An atoll is a ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef surrounding a central lagoon. Lakshadweep and Maldives provide examples.
22.tq: Apply the characteristic-shape clue to identify the landform.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Submarine canyon — Deep, steep-sided valley cut across the shelf and slope
Guyot — Coral reef surrounding a lagoon
Atoll — Flat-topped seamount planed by waves
Seamount — Valley formed off a river mouth
22.x: A submarine canyon is a deep, steep-sided valley that cuts across the continental shelf and slope, often near river mouths.
22.tq: Start with the sure definition and eliminate the options with swapped landforms.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s: The Mahadevan Canyon, mentioned in relation to submarine canyons, is located off the coast of:
22.x: Mahadevan Canyon is a submarine canyon located off Visakhapatnam.
22.tq: Test the location attached to a named geographical feature.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s:
With reference to the Deep Ocean Mission surveys, consider the following statements:
1. About 25 seamounts in the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal were surveyed.
2. About 39 potentially new species were found.
3. Two active and two inactive hydrothermal vents were found.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: All three statements are correct: the surveys covered about 25 seamounts, identified about 39 potentially new species, and found two active and two inactive hydrothermal vents.
22.tq: Retain all the numerical details and test them together through coded statements.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s: Which one of the following was declared a critical habitat by CMS COP15?
22.x: CMS COP15 declared seamounts to be critical habitat.
22.tq: Use the named-organisation and feature association to avoid a location-based distractor.
22.sec: Minor relief - seamounts, guyots, atolls, canyons

22.s: Trenches in the ocean floor primarily mark:
o: Locations where ocean water freezes permanently
The margins of stable continental interiors
Zones where one tectonic plate dives beneath another
22.x: Oceanic trenches commonly occur at subduction zones, where one plate descends beneath another.
22.tq: Apply the landform-process relationship rather than recalling only a name.
22.sec: Trenches → ocean, deepest point of each ocean

22.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
