2. Advancing Indian Standard Time by 30 minutes.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
33.x: Both proposals have been discussed: a separate North-Eastern time zone and advancing IST by 30 minutes.
33.tq: Recognise both stated alternatives instead of treating the time-zone debate as a settled policy.

33.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
33.x: Guhar Moti in Gujarat's Kutch region is the westernmost point listed for India. Kibithu is in the east, Indira Col is in the north and Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.
33.tq: Test direction-place confusions by separating the easternmost and westernmost points.

33.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Its area is approximately 1,62,970 square kilometres.
2. It accounts for about 4.96 per cent of India's area.
3. It ranks seventh among the Indian States in area.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh has an area of about 1,62,970 square kilometres, represents approximately 4.96 per cent of India's area, and ranks seventh by area.
33.tq: Use the coded statement format to connect the area, percentage and rank without treating them as isolated figures.

33.s: The latitudinal extent of the present State of Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
33.x: The latitudinal extent of present-day Andhra Pradesh is approximately 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N. An extent reaching 22° N is not applicable to the present State of Andhra Pradesh.
33.tq: Check the precise latitude limits and reject the broader, outdated-looking range.

33.s: The coastline of Andhra Pradesh, according to the 2023–24 remeasurement, is approximately:
o: 974 km, ranking fourth among coastal States
1,162.97 km, ranking third after Gujarat and Maharashtra
1,053.07 km, ranking third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu
33.x: The 2023–24 remeasurement places Andhra Pradesh's coastline at approximately 1,053.07 km, making it the third-longest after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
33.tq: Distinguish the latest remeasurement from the earlier coastline figure and verify both the value and rank.

33.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the earlier and revised coastline figures associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: 974 km in APSES 2024–25 and 1,053.07 km after the 2023–24 remeasurement
1,053.07 km in APSES 2024–25 and 974 km after the 2023–24 remeasurement
974 km in both APSES 2024–25 and the 2023–24 remeasurement
1,053.07 km in both APSES 2024–25 and the 2023–24 remeasurement
33.x: The APSES 2024–25 figure is 974 km, while the 2023–24 remeasurement gives 1,053.07 km. The revised figure is associated with Andhra Pradesh's present third position after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
33.tq: Discriminate between two close numerical figures by attaching each one to its correct reference period.

33.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The debate over a single time zone in India includes a proposal for a separate time zone for the North-Eastern region.
2. The question of a separate North-Eastern time zone is discussed in relation to India's geographical extent and time differences.
3. India has already adopted a separate official time zone exclusively for the North-Eastern States.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: The issue is a continuing debate between retaining a single time zone and introducing a separate North-Eastern time zone. India has not already adopted such a separate official time zone.
33.tq: Identify the false statement created by converting a policy debate into an accomplished fact.

33.s: Which of the following statements about India's international land borders is correct?
o: Bangladesh and Afghanistan share equal-length land borders with India.
Afghanistan shares India's longest land border, while Bangladesh shares the shortest.
The longest land border is with Afghanistan, whereas the shortest is with Bangladesh.
Bangladesh shares India's longest land border, while Afghanistan shares the shortest among the listed neighbouring countries.
33.x: Among the comparisons specified, Bangladesh has the longest land border with India and Afghanistan has the shortest.
33.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by checking which neighbouring country is placed at each extreme.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the standard west-to-east regional division of the Himalayas with their bounding rivers?
o: Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Sutlej; Kumaon Himalaya—Sutlej to Kali; Nepal Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang
Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Beas; Kumaon Himalaya—Beas to Kali; Nepal Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang
Punjab Himalaya—Jhelum to Sutlej; Kumaon Himalaya—Sutlej to Gandak; Nepal Himalaya—Gandak to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Lohit
Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Kali; Kumaon Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Nepal Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang; Assam Himalaya—Dihang to Lohit
34.x: The standard Burrard boundaries are Indus–Sutlej, Sutlej–Kali, Kali–Teesta and Teesta–Dihang. The Punjab Himalaya is sometimes extended up to the Beas in some accounts, but Sutlej is the standard boundary.
34.tq: Start from the sure river pair and eliminate options that shift the regional boundaries.

34.s: The Punjab Himalaya is chiefly associated with which of the following groups of peaks?
34.x: Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh are prominent peaks of the Punjab or Kashmir-Himachal Himalaya.
34.tq: Use the regional-division cluster to associate each division with its characteristic peaks.

34.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kumaon Himalaya — Sutlej to Kali — Nainital and Bhimtal
Nepal Himalaya — Indus to Sutlej — Everest and Kanchenjunga
Assam Himalaya — Kali to Teesta — Namcha Barwa
Punjab Himalaya — Teesta to Dihang — Nanga Parbat
34.x: The Kumaon Himalaya lies between the Sutlej and Kali and includes the lakes Nainital and Bhimtal. Everest and Kanchenjunga belong to the Nepal Himalayan sector, while Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya.
34.tq: Match the boundary rivers with the distinctive geographical features of the same division.

34.s: The Kumaon Himalaya is particularly associated with which of the following glaciers?
34.x: Pindari, Milam and Kafni glaciers are associated with the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
34.tq: Test a distinctive list through direct recall rather than confusing it with Trans-Himalayan glaciers.

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the parallel ranges of the Himalayas:
1. The Karakoram is part of the Trans-Himalaya.
2. The Ladakh Range continues eastwards into Tibet as the Kailash Range.
3. The Zaskar Range lies south of the Karakoram and is separated from the Pir Panjal by the Kashmir Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. Karakoram and Zaskar are Trans-Himalayan ranges, Ladakh continues as Kailash in Tibet, and the Kashmir Valley separates Zaskar from Pir Panjal.
34.tq: Check each range by its position and continuation before selecting the coded combination.

34.s:
Arrange the following Himalayan ranges from north to south:
A. Himachal
B. Karakoram
C. Shiwalik
D. Himadri
E. Ladakh
34.x: From north to south, the sequence is Karakoram, Ladakh, Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik.
34.tq: Fix the northernmost Trans-Himalayan range first, then move southward through the three principal Himalayan ranges.

34.s: Which one of the following statements about the Himadri is correct?
o: It is the youngest and narrowest Himalayan range.
It lies south of the Shiwalik and contains simple Jura-type folds.
It is the loftiest and oldest Himalayan range and has a granite core.
It has an average elevation of about 1,300 metres and consists mainly of river deposits.
34.x: The Himadri, or Greater Himalaya, is the loftiest and oldest Himalayan range, with an average elevation above 6,000 metres and a granite core.
34.tq: Use the contrast between the oldest, loftiest Himadri and the youngest, narrowest Shiwalik.

34.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Himachal or Lesser Himalaya?
o: Pir Panjal — Jhelum-Beas sector — approximately 300 km
34.x: Pir Panjal is a major range of the Himachal Himalaya extending for about 300 km in the Jhelum-Beas sector. Dhauladhar, Mussoorie and Mahabharat are also associated with the Lesser Himalaya.
34.tq: Pair the range with the correct parallel belt and approximate extent.

34.s: The Shiwalik Range is best described as a range that is
o: the loftiest range with an average elevation above 6,000 metres
a Trans-Himalayan range extending into Tibet
the oldest, widest and composed mainly of granite
the youngest and narrowest, with simple Jura-type folds of river deposits
34.x: The Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest Himalayan range, about 15–50 km wide, with an average elevation of about 1,300 metres and simple folds formed from river deposits.
34.tq: Compare age, width, elevation and composition to distinguish the Shiwalik from the other ranges.

34.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Trans-Himalaya?
o: It was formed after the main Himalayan ranges and contains the lowest plateau of India.
It was formed before the Himalayas, and the Ladakh Plateau is the highest plateau in India.
It lies south of the Himadri and is younger than the Shiwalik.
It consists only of the Shiwalik and Himachal ranges.
34.x: The Trans-Himalaya formed before the Himalayas. The Ladakh Plateau is regarded as the highest plateau in India.
34.tq: Use the age comparison and the distinctive superlative associated with the Ladakh Plateau.

34.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
34.x: Kashmir, Kangra and Kullu valleys lie in the Himachal or Lesser Himalaya. Kashmir Valley is not a valley of the Shiwalik Range.
34.tq: Find the one location assigned to the wrong parallel range.

34.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
34.x: Patli Dun is located in Uttarakhand. Kotli Dun and Nalagarh Dun are associated with Himachal Pradesh, while Dehradun is in Uttarakhand.
34.tq: Use state-location matching to separate the similarly named Himalayan duns.

34.s: Karewas of the Kashmir Valley are best described as
o: marine sediments of the Tethys Sea used for rubber cultivation
glacial moraines of the Shiwalik Range used for jute cultivation
volcanic cones used for tea cultivation
lacustrine deposits of Pleistocene age used for saffron cultivation
34.x: Karewas are lake or lacustrine deposits in the Kashmir Valley. They are of Pleistocene age and are important for saffron cultivation.
34.tq: Identify the landform from its origin, age and characteristic agricultural use.

34.s: Which one of the following peaks is correctly matched with its range and location?
34.x: Kamet is a peak of the Himadri in the Kumaon or Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand. Dhaulagiri is in Nepal, Namcha Barwa is in the Assam Himalaya of Tibet, and Kailash belongs to the Trans-Himalaya.
34.tq: Start with the peak whose range, regional division and country are all precisely aligned.

34.s: Which of the following statements regarding Kanchenjunga is correct?
o: It is wholly within Nepal and belongs to the Punjab Himalaya.
It marks the western end of the Assam Himalaya in Tibet.
It lies in the Himadri on the India-Nepal boundary and is the highest peak wholly in India.
It is located in the Karakoram under Pakistan-China control.
34.x: Kanchenjunga belongs to the Himadri and lies on the India-Nepal boundary. It is the highest peak wholly in India, although it is not entirely within India.
34.tq: Distinguish “highest peak wholly in India” from the highest peak associated with India’s claim.

34.s: Godwin Austen, commonly known as K2, is correctly described as
o: a peak of the Himadri, 8,586 metres high, wholly within Uttarakhand
a peak of the Nepal Himalaya, 8,611 metres high, wholly within Nepal
a peak of the Karakoram, 8,611 metres high, under Pakistan-China control and second highest in the world
a peak of the Assam Himalaya, 8,586 metres high, located in Tibet
34.x: Godwin Austen or K2 is 8,611 metres high and belongs to the Karakoram. It lies in territory under Pakistan-China control and is the world’s second-highest peak.
34.tq: Separate the peak’s height, range, political control and world ranking instead of relying on a single superlative.

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nanga Parbat — eastern end of Assam Himalaya — China
Namcha Barwa — eastern end of Assam Himalaya — Tibet
Dhaulagiri — western end of Punjab Himalaya — Pakistan
34.x: Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya and is located in Tibet, China. Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayan arc in the Punjab Himalaya.
34.tq: Use the western-end/eastern-end contrast to eliminate the swapped peak-location pairs.

34.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Nanda Devi — Himadri, Kumaon Himalaya — Uttarakhand
34.x: Nanda Devi is a peak of the Greater Himalaya in the Kumaon Himalaya and is located in Uttarakhand. Dhaulagiri is in the Nepal Himalaya.
34.tq: Check the peak against both its Himalayan division and its state or country.

34.s: The Himalayan arc extends approximately from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa over a length of
34.x: The Himalayan arc extends for approximately 2,414 km from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namcha Barwa in the east.
34.tq: Choose the precise length rather than the rounded distractor values.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the variation in the width of the Himalayas?
o: About 50 km in Kashmir and 1,000 km in Arunachal Pradesh
About 500 km in Kashmir and 200 km in Arunachal Pradesh
About 400 km throughout the entire Himalayan arc
About 200 km in Kashmir and 500 km in Arunachal Pradesh
34.x: The Himalayas are wider in Kashmir, where their width is about 500 km, and narrower in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is about 200 km.
34.tq: Watch for the reversed west-to-east comparison in the distractors.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the Himalayas:
1. The folds of the Himadri are asymmetrical.
2. The steep slope of the Himalayas faces the plains.
3. The gentler slope faces Tibet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. The Himadri has asymmetrical folds; the Himalayan slope towards the plains is steeper, while the Tibetan side is gentler.
34.tq: Test the complete structural pattern and avoid reversing the two slopes.

34.s: The uplift of the Himalayas is associated with Tethys sediments and occurred mainly during the
o: Eocene to Pliocene period of the Tertiary
34.x: The Himalayas were uplifted from Tethys sediments during the Tertiary, broadly from the Eocene to the Pliocene, approximately 60 to 7 million years ago.
34.tq: Link the geological material, period and approximate time span in one sequence.

34.s: The collision responsible for the formation and continued uplift of the Himalayas occurred between the
34.x: The Indian Plate collided with the Eurasian Plate approximately 4–5 crore years ago. The Himalayas are still rising because tectonic convergence continues.
34.tq: Identify the two plates directly involved rather than selecting another major tectonic plate.

34.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four major structural zones of the Himalayas?
34.x: The four structural zones are the Indus-Tsangpo Suture Zone, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault. Great Rift Valley Zone is not included in this classification.
34.tq: Recall the named structural list and identify the outside term.

34.s: The Himalayan range takes a sharp knee-bend near Namcha Barwa at the
34.x: The Himalaya makes a knee-bend at the Dihang gorge near Namcha Barwa and then turns southwards as the Purvanchal hills.
34.tq: Associate the distinctive geomorphic change in direction with its exact gorge and peak.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
34.x: Patkai Bum lies in Arunachal Pradesh along the Myanmar border. Naga Hills are in Nagaland, Manipur Hills in Manipur and Mizo Hills in Mizoram.
34.tq: Use state-hill matching and eliminate the systematic state swaps.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: Which of the following statements about the Purvanchal hills is correct?
o: They extend from Kashmir to Himachal Pradesh without entering the North-East.
They are the southern continuation of the Himalayas after the Dihang knee-bend and generally range from 500 to 3,000 metres in height.
They are formed by a westward turn of the Himalayas at the Sutlej gorge.
They consist exclusively of the Shiwalik hills of Uttarakhand.
34.x: After the knee-bend near Namcha Barwa and the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas turn south as the Purvanchal hills. Their heights generally range from 500 to 3,000 metres.
34.tq: Apply the direction-change clue and the elevation range to identify the Purvanchal description.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Barail Range — links Naga and Mizo hills — highest range of Assam
34.x: The Barail Range links the Naga and Mizo hills and is the highest range of Assam. Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills belong to Meghalaya and form part of the Shillong Plateau.
34.tq: Begin with the distinctive Barail description and reject options that interchange the North-Eastern states.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills are associated with the
o: Ladakh Plateau of Jammu and Kashmir
34.x: Garo, Khasi and Jaintia are the principal hill groups associated with the Shillong Plateau in Meghalaya.
34.tq: Use the three-hill group as a distinctive geographical cluster.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the alignment of the major Purvanchal hill groups?
o: Garo-Khasi-Jaintia run east-west, while the Mizo and Rakhine hills run north-south.
All the hill groups run exclusively west-east.
All the hill groups form a single east-west range without intersection.
Naga and Mizo hills run east-west, while Garo-Khasi-Jaintia run north-south.
34.x: The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills generally run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills. The specified contrast is correctly stated in option a.
34.tq: Compare the two directional alignments rather than treating all North-Eastern hills as one trend.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: The Molasse Basin in the Indian Himalayan context is associated with
34.x: The Molasse Basin is associated with Mizoram and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
34.tq: Pair the basin with its state and characteristic material.
34.sec: Purvanchal hills and the Molasse basin

34.s: How many broad groups are included under the classification of the northern mountains based on relief and alignment?
34.x: The northern mountains are classified into three broad groups: the Himalayas, the Trans-Himalayas and the Purvanchal.
34.tq: Distinguish the count of broad northern-mountain groups from the separate regional and structural counts.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the three longitudinal parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
34.x: The three principal longitudinal parallel ranges are Himadri or Greater Himalaya, Himachal or Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik or Outer Himalaya.
34.tq: Separate the longitudinal-range classification from the regional west-to-east classification.

34.s: The Himalayas are divided into how many broad regional divisions extending from west to east?
34.x: The four west-to-east regional divisions are Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal and Assam Himalaya.
34.tq: Use the named regional sequence to confirm the count rather than confusing it with the three parallel ranges.

34.s: Which one of the following represents the correct classification by the three principal bases mentioned for the northern mountain system?
o: Northern mountains—3; longitudinal parallel ranges—3; regional divisions—4; structural zones—4
Northern mountains—4; longitudinal parallel ranges—3; regional divisions—3; structural zones—5
Northern mountains—3; longitudinal parallel ranges—4; regional divisions—4; structural zones—3
Northern mountains—5; longitudinal parallel ranges—4; regional divisions—3; structural zones—4
34.x: The counts are three northern-mountain groups, three longitudinal parallel ranges, four regional divisions and four structural zones.
34.tq: Compare the four counts together and reject options that interchange the two threes and two fours.

34.s: Approximately what proportion of India's area is occupied by plains according to the stated relief-share classification?
34.x: Plains form the largest relief division of India and account for about 43 percent of the country’s area.
34.tq: Choose the precise approximate share and avoid shifting the stated percentage by ten points.

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Himalayan mountain passes:
1. Zoji La lies in the Zaskar sector of Ladakh and connects Srinagar with Leh.
2. Banihal Pass is located in the Pir Panjal Range and connects Jammu with Srinagar.
3. Shipki La is associated with the entry of the Sutlej into India and provides access towards Tibet.
4. Nathu La connects Gangtok with Tibet through the Chumbi Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All four statements are correct. Zoji La, Banihal, Shipki La and Nathu La have the stated locations and connecting routes.
34.tq: Use the pass–route association and check each statement independently.

34.s: The heights of Banihal Pass and Rohtang Pass are approximately
34.x: Banihal Pass has an elevation of about 2,833 metres, whereas Rohtang Pass has an elevation of about 3,978 metres.
34.tq: Compare the numerical values directly and watch for reversal of the pair.

34.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of avalanche-prone Himalayan passes?
o: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana
Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La and Bomdi La
Lipulekh, Banihal, Zoji La and Shipki La
Rohtang, Nathu La, Bomdi La and Lipulekh
34.x: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana are identified as avalanche-prone passes.
34.tq: Identify the complete group rather than selecting a familiar individual pass.

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nathu La — Gangtok-Tibet route through the Chumbi Valley
34.x: Nathu La connects Gangtok with Tibet through the Chumbi Valley. The other routes are associated with Zoji La, Shipki La and Banihal respectively.
34.tq: Start from the sure pass–route pair and eliminate the swapped connections.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about glaciers:
1. Siachen Glacier is situated in the Karakoram Range, in the Nubra region.
2. Siachen marks the northern limit of Ladakh.
3. Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar glaciers are located in Gilgit-Baltistan in the Karakoram region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. Siachen lies in the Karakoram's Nubra region and marks Ladakh's northern limit, while Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar are in the Karakoram sector of Gilgit-Baltistan.
34.tq: Group glaciers by their range and position before evaluating the statements.

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
34.x: Baltoro Glacier belongs to the Karakoram Range, not the Greater Himalaya. Gangotri is in the Greater Himalaya, while Pindari and Milam are associated with the Kumaon region.
34.tq: Find the single reversed glacier–range association.

34.s: Gangotri Glacier is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Pir Panjal Range and source of the Chenab
Kumaon Range and source of the Mandakini
Greater Himalaya and source of the Bhagirathi
34.x: Gangotri Glacier is located in the Greater Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh.
34.tq: Match the glacier with both its range and its associated river source.

34.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Glacier)
a. Siachen
b. Baltoro
c. Gangotri
d. Pindari

List-II (Range or region)
i. Kumaon
 ii. Greater Himalaya
 iii. Karakoram, Nubra region
 iv. Karakoram, Gilgit-Baltistan
34.x: Siachen is in the Karakoram's Nubra region, Baltoro is in Karakoram in Gilgit-Baltistan, Gangotri belongs to the Greater Himalaya, and Pindari belongs to Kumaon.
34.tq: Start from the distinctive Siachen–Nubra and Gangotri–Greater Himalaya pairs.

34.s:
The Himalayas are significant to India because they
1. form India's northern boundary.
2. act as a climatic barrier.
3. have contributed debris that helped build the Indo-Gangetic Plain through the Shiwalik system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. The Himalayas define India's northern boundary, act as a climatic barrier, and Shiwalik debris contributed to the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
34.tq: Treat geographical significance as a cause-and-effect set rather than as isolated facts.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the Himadri and the Shiwalik ranges?
o: Himadri is the oldest and loftiest, whereas Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest.
Himadri is the youngest and narrowest, whereas Shiwalik is the oldest and loftiest.
Both Himadri and Shiwalik are the oldest and loftiest ranges.
Both Himadri and Shiwalik are the youngest and narrowest ranges.
34.x: The Himadri is described as the oldest and loftiest Himalayan range, while the Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest.
34.tq: Check both sides of the comparison; reversed adjectives form the main distractor.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the western and eastern ends of the Himalayas respectively?
34.x: Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayas, while Namcha Barwa marks their eastern end.
34.tq: Use the first–last method for geographical end-point questions.

34.s:
Assertion (A): The Shiwalik range has an important role in the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
Reason (R): The Shiwaliks consist largely of debris derived from the Himalayan ranges.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
34.x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the debris carried and deposited from the Himalayan ranges explains the Shiwalik contribution to the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
34.tq: Test whether the reason explains the stated geographical effect, not merely whether both facts are true.

35.s: Which one of the following coastal regions extends from Goa to Mangaluru?
35.x: The Kannad or Karnataka Coast extends from Goa to Mangaluru.
35.tq: Directly identify the coastal segment from its terminal points.
35.sec: Coastal plains - divisions, width, lagoons, emergent vs submergent

35.s: The Kannad Coast has an approximate length and width of
35.x: The Kannad Coast is about 255 km long and 8–24 km wide.
35.tq: Match the numerical pair with the correct geographical feature.
35.sec: Coastal plains - divisions, width, lagoons, emergent vs submergent

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Malabar Coast:
1. It extends from Mangaluru to Kanyakumari.
2. It is approximately 550 km long.
3. Its width generally varies from 10 to 30 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: The Malabar Coast extends from Mangaluru to Kanyakumari, is about 550 km long and is generally 10–30 km wide.
35.tq: Check all numerical and boundary statements before selecting the combined code.
35.sec: Coastal plains - divisions, width, lagoons, emergent vs submergent

35.s: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the Kannad Coast?
o: Broad deltas formed by the Mahanadi and Krishna
Extensive dry plains of Tamil Nadu
Spurs of the Western Ghats reaching the coast
35.x: Spurs of the Western Ghats reach the coast in the Kannad region.
35.tq: Use the distinctive physical feature to discriminate between neighbouring coastal divisions.
35.sec: Coastal plains - divisions, width, lagoons, emergent vs submergent

35.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Northern Circars — Dry coast without deltas
35.x: The Nal Lake depression is associated with the Kachchh-Kathiawar coastal region. The Malabar is narrow and wet, the Coromandel is broad and dry, and the Northern Circars have broad deltas.
35.tq: Start from the distinctive place-feature pair and eliminate reversed characteristics.

35.s: Girnar, the highest feature of the Kachchh-Kathiawar region, is described as a
35.x: Girnar is an extinct volcano, while the Mandav Hills are also associated with the Kachchh-Kathiawar region.
35.tq: Test the geological origin of a named landform rather than its location alone.

35.s:

36.x: Nepal flash floods raised the Narayani-Gandak system, leading to alerts in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
36.tq: Link the flood source, river system and affected states in a current geographical event.
36.sec: Universal angles

36.s:
Which of the following factors has been identified as partly contributing to the man-made component of Brahmaputra floods?
1. Roads constructed without adequate drainage
2. Deforestation
3. Silted river channels
4. Increased formation of glacial cirques
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Roads without adequate drainage, deforestation and silted channels are cited as partly man-made contributors to Brahmaputra flooding. Glacial cirques are not included among these factors.
36.tq: Separate human-induced flood factors from an unrelated glacial landform.
36.sec: Universal angles

36.s: Which one of the following is the easternmost tributary of the Ganga?
36.x: The Mahananda is identified as the easternmost tributary of the Ganga.
36.tq: Use the directional superlative directly and distinguish it from the westernmost tributary.
36.sec: Universal angles

36.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a distinctive geographical description?
36.x: Majuli is identified as the largest riverine island. Mahananda is the easternmost Ganga tributary, Yamuna the westernmost, and Loktak is a freshwater lake of Manipur.
36.tq: Compare several superlatives and distinctive descriptions while rejecting reversed directional labels.
36.sec: Universal angles

37.s: Which one of the following is the largest left-bank tributary of the Godavari?
37.x: Pranhita is the largest left-bank tributary of the Godavari. It is formed by the Wardha and Wainganga rivers and joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram.
37.tq: Use the size clue to distinguish the major tributary from other left-bank tributaries.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indravati — Godavari
2. Tel — Mahanadi
3. Kabini — Krishna
4. Tungabhadra — Krishna
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
37.x: Indravati is a tributary of the Godavari, while Tel and Tungabhadra are tributaries of the Mahanadi and Krishna respectively. Kabini is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri, not the Krishna.
37.tq: Split the options by checking the easily confusable river–tributary pair.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s: With reference to the Godavari, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Pravara, Manjira and Manair are its right-bank tributaries.
Purna, Pranahita and Sabari are its right-bank tributaries.
Tungabhadra is its largest left-bank tributary.
Tel is its principal right-bank tributary.
37.x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right bank. Purna, Pranahita, Indravati and Sabari are its important left-bank tributaries.
37.tq: Test the left-bank and right-bank classification directly.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (River)
a. Bhima
b. Kabini
c. Tel
 d. Hemavathi

List-II (Main river)
i. Kaveri
ii. Mahanadi
iii. Krishna
iv. Krishna

Codes:
37.x: Bhima is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna; Kabini and Hemavathi are tributaries of the Kaveri; and Tel is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi.
37.tq: Start from the sure pair Kabini–Kaveri and eliminate incompatible codes.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
37.x: Ghataprabha is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna. Tungabhadra is also a right-bank tributary, Sheonath is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi, and Bhavani is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri.
37.tq: Find the correctly matched river and bank among reversed bank classifications.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s: Vedavathi, formed by the Veda and Avathi streams in the Bababudangiri hills, is a right-bank tributary of which river?
37.x: Vedavathi is a right-bank tributary of the Tungabhadra and joins it at Siruguppa.
37.tq: Use the tributary–sub-tributary relationship rather than confusing it with a direct Krishna tributary.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the east-flowing rivers of Peninsular India is correct?
o: They generally form large deltas at their mouths.
They invariably flow through rift valleys and form estuaries.
They all originate in the Eastern Ghats.
They are short and swift and are mainly used for natural harbours.
37.x: East-flowing rivers generally drain into the Bay of Bengal and form large deltas. West-flowing rivers more commonly form estuaries and support hydropower and natural harbours.
37.tq: Use the mouth feature to separate east-flowing rivers from west-flowing rivers.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of west-flowing rivers?
37.x: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati and Mahi flow westwards towards the Arabian Sea. The other groups contain east-flowing rivers.
37.tq: Classify the entire group by its drainage direction before examining individual rivers.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Narmada flows through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
2. Tapi flows through a rift valley between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges.
3. Both Narmada and Tapi form large deltas at their mouths.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys, but as west-flowing rivers they generally form estuaries rather than large deltas.
37.tq: Identify the false statement by reversing the characteristic mouth of west-flowing rivers.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following rivers is the longest west-flowing river of India?
37.x: Narmada is the longest west-flowing river, with a length of about 1,312 km. Tapi is the second longest at about 724 km.
37.tq: Distinguish the longest river from the second-ranked river using the stated lengths.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: The Tapi river reaches the Arabian Sea at which of the following places?
o: Kandla near the Gulf of Kachchh
Diu near the Gulf of Khambhat
37.x: The Tapi reaches the sea at Suvali near Surat. It is the second longest west-flowing peninsular river and runs through a rift valley.
37.tq: Use the precise mouth location to distinguish Tapi from other west-flowing rivers.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following rivers crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat?
37.x: The Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and ultimately reaches the Gulf of Khambhat.
37.tq: Combine the unusual numerical crossing fact with the destination to identify the river.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following is an inland-drainage river?
37.x: Luni is an inland-drainage river that ends in the Rann of Kutch. Other inland-drainage rivers listed include Machhu, Rupen, Saraswati, Banas and Ghaggar.
37.tq: Recognise the river that does not reach the sea but terminates in an inland basin.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
2. Banas is an east-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
3. Sahibi is a north-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
4. Sabarmati is a west-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: All four statements are correct. The Aravallis give rise to west-flowing Luni and Sabarmati, east-flowing Banas and north-flowing Sahibi; Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
37.tq: Use directional classification to verify each Aravalli-born river.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Approximately how many small rivers drain the west coast of India?
37.x: About 600 small rivers drain the west coast. These rivers are generally short and swift and commonly form estuaries.
37.tq: Retain the approximate figure rather than confusing it with the lengths of major rivers.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s:
Arrange the following Peninsular rivers in descending order of their lengths:
A. Mahanadi
B. Tapi
C. Godavari
D. Narmada
37.x: The descending order is Godavari (1,465 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
37.tq: Arrange by the numerical hierarchy, starting with the longest river and ending with the shortest.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the longest Peninsular rivers in descending order?
37.x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
37.tq: Compare adjacent river lengths instead of relying only on whether they flow east or west.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: The Narmada and Son rivers originate from which of the following places?
37.x: Both the Narmada and Son originate at Amarkantak in the Maikal range of Madhya Pradesh.
37.tq: Link the common source with the two rivers rather than selecting a source associated with only one river.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
37.x: The Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats, at the Krishna Kund. The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar, Mahanadi at Sihawa and Tapi at Multai.
37.tq: Match each river with its distinctive source and eliminate the swapped-source pairs.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: The source of the Kaveri is located at which of the following places?
o: Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu
37.x: The Kaveri rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu, Karnataka. Nandi hills are associated with the origin of the Pennar.
37.tq: Separate the closely located Karnataka source regions of Kaveri and Pennar.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
37.x: The Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar. The Brahmagiri hills at Talakaveri are the source of the Kaveri.
37.tq: Find the swapped source by comparing the Western Ghats source points.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s:
Which of the following rivers originate in the Eastern Ghats?
1. Vamsadhara
2. Nagavali
3. Machkund
4. Sileru
5. Sabari
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru and Sabari are all listed as rivers originating in the Eastern Ghats.
37.tq: When every listed item belongs to the same source region, select the complete combination.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: The river Tapi originates at which of the following places?
o: Multai in the Satpura plateau of Betul district
37.x: The Tapi rises at Multai, near Betul, in the Satpura plateau of Madhya Pradesh.
37.tq: Use the precise source locality to distinguish Tapi from Narmada, Mahanadi and Kaveri.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: The Western Ghats are called the ‘Water Tower of Peninsular India’ mainly because they provide the sources of which group of rivers?
37.x: The Western Ghats are described as the Water Tower of Peninsular India because they provide the sources of the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri river systems.
37.tq: Connect the descriptive geographical title with the river systems originating in the region.
37.sec: River origin → source hills/plateau  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following statements about west-flowing rivers is correct?
o: They are generally short and swift and are suitable for hydropower generation.
They generally have long courses and form extensive deltas.
They invariably terminate in inland salt lakes.
They flow only through the Eastern Ghats.
37.x: West-flowing rivers are generally short and swift, form estuaries rather than deltas and are suitable for hydropower. Their estuaries also support natural harbours on the west coast.
37.tq: Select the option containing the complete characteristic combination of west-flowing rivers.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Narmada — Marble Rocks and Dhuandhar Falls near Jabalpur
37.x: Luni is an Aravalli-born desert river that ends in the Rann of Kutch, not the Gulf of Khambhat. Narmada, Tapi and Periyar are correctly matched with the other descriptions.
37.tq: Use the destination trap to distinguish inland-drainage Luni from west-flowing rivers reaching the sea.
37.sec: West-flowing vs east-flowing, rift valleys, inland drainage  [APPSC]

37.s: Which one of the following sets contains only left-bank tributaries of the Mahanadi and Godavari respectively?
o: Hasdeo and Tel; Pranahita and Manair
Tel and Sheonath; Pravara and Manjira
Sheonath and Hasdeo; Purna and Indravati
Sheonath and Tel; Sabari and Pravara
37.x: Sheonath and Hasdeo are left-bank tributaries of the Mahanadi, while Purna and Indravati are left-bank tributaries of the Godavari. Tel is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi, and Pravara and Manjira are right-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
37.tq: Check the bank classification separately for each main river before combining the pairs.
37.sec: Tributaries → main river and bank  [APPSC]

37.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the 12 major river basins of India, each having an area exceeding 20,000 sq km?
37.x: Periyar is not included in the list of India's 12 major basins given here. The list includes Mahi, Sabarmati and Brahmani-Baitarani.
37.tq: Find the one item outside the named classification.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the relative size of river basins in Peninsular India:
1. The Godavari basin is larger than the Krishna basin.
2. The Krishna basin is larger than the Mahanadi basin.
3. The Narmada and Kaveri basins are approximately equal in size.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: The relative order is Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi, while the Narmada and Kaveri basins are approximately equal in size.
37.tq: Use the comparison chain and identify the coded combination.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s:
Arrange the following rivers in descending order of their length:
A. Krishna
B. Narmada
C. Godavari
D. Mahanadi
37.x: The descending order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km) and Mahanadi (858 km).
37.tq: Arrange the items using the numerical ranking from longest to shortest.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
37.x: The Narmada is 1,312 km long. The Ganga is 2,525 km, the Godavari 1,465 km, the Krishna 1,400 km and the Kaveri 805 km long.
37.tq: Start from the sure river-length pair.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Brahmaputra is longer overall than the Ganga.
2. Only about 885 km of the Brahmaputra lies in India.
3. The Ganga is regarded as India's longest river.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: The Brahmaputra is about 2,900 km long overall, but only 885 km lies in India. The Ganga, at 2,525 km, is considered India's longest river.
37.tq: Separate overall length from length within India.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s: India's river-basin classification comprises which of the following?
37.x: India has 20 basins: 12 major basins with areas over 20,000 sq km each and 8 composite basins.
37.tq: Recall the paired numerical classification.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna basin is correct?
o: It is the largest basin of India.
It is smaller than the Godavari basin.
It is the smallest major basin of India.
37.x: The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna basin is the largest basin of India. The Ganga alone covers approximately 9,51,600 sq km.
37.tq: Reject reversed comparison statements.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

37.s: The Godavari river is popularly known as which of the following?
37.x: The Godavari is known as Dakshin Ganga or Dakshina Ganga. The name Dakshina Ganga is also used for the Kaveri in some references.
37.tq: Discriminate between similar names associated with Peninsular rivers.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s:
Which of the following waterfalls is correctly matched with its river and state?
1. Kunchikal — Varahi — Karnataka
2. Jog — Sharavati — Karnataka
3. Dhuandhar — Narmada — Madhya Pradesh
4. Hundru — Subarnarekha — Jharkhand
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: All four pairs are correct. Kunchikal is on the Varahi, Jog on the Sharavati, Dhuandhar on the Narmada and Hundru on the Subarnarekha.
37.tq: Verify each waterfall–river–state linkage before selecting the code.
37.sec: Waterfalls → river and region

37.s: Dudhsagar Falls is situated on the Mandovi River near which geographical location?
37.x: Dudhsagar Falls lies on the Mandovi River near the Goa–Karnataka border.
37.tq: Combine the river and location clues.
37.sec: Waterfalls → river and region

37.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
37.x: Jog Falls is on the Sharavati River in Karnataka, not on the Mandovi River in Goa. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
37.tq: Find the swapped river–waterfall association.
37.sec: Waterfalls → river and region

37.s:
Which of the following waterfalls are associated with the Kaveri River?
1. Sivasamudram
2. Chunchanakatte
3. Hogenakkal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Sivasamudram, Chunchanakatte and Hogenakkal are all waterfalls associated with the Kaveri River.
37.tq: Group the items by their common river association.
37.sec: Waterfalls → river and region

37.s: Dhuandhar Falls is located near which of the following places?
o: Ranchi and the Chota Nagpur Plateau
37.x: Dhuandhar Falls is situated on the Narmada near Jabalpur, close to the Marble Rocks, in Madhya Pradesh.
37.tq: Use the waterfall–landform–location combination.
37.sec: Waterfalls → river and region

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
37.x: Lonar in Maharashtra is a saline-alkaline lake formed in a meteorite-impact crater.
37.tq: Start with the distinctive origin-based lake pair.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s: Chilika Lake is best described as which of the following?
o: A freshwater lake on the Jhelum
A saline-alkaline crater lake in Maharashtra
37.x: Chilika in Odisha is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon and was India's first Ramsar site in 1981.
37.tq: Distinguish lagoon, freshwater lake and crater lake categories.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sambhar — Rajasthan — Inland saline lake
2. Didwana — Rajasthan — Saline lake
3. Vembanad — Kerala — Brackish backwater
4. Kolleru — Andhra Pradesh — Freshwater lake
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: All four pairs are correct. Sambhar and Didwana are in Rajasthan, Vembanad is in Kerala, and Kolleru is Andhra Pradesh's major freshwater lake.
37.tq: Check each lake against both its state and water type.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s: Which one of the following is an artificial lake?
o: A lake formed by dam construction
37.x: A lake formed by dam construction is an artificial lake. Lonar is a meteorite-impact lake, Sambhar is an inland saline lake and Kolleru is a natural freshwater lake.
37.tq: Apply the definition of an artificial lake rather than recalling a place name.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s: Pulicat Lake is correctly described as which of the following?
o: India's second-largest brackish lagoon, shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
A saline lake in northern Rajasthan
A freshwater lake wholly within Andhra Pradesh
37.x: Pulicat is a brackish lagoon shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and is regarded as India's second-largest brackish lagoon.
37.tq: Discriminate Pulicat from Kolleru by type and state relationship.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s: Wular Lake is situated on which river and between which ranges?
o: Kaveri; Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats
37.x: Wular is a freshwater lake on the Jhelum, situated between the Pir Panjal and Zaskar ranges.
37.tq: Combine the waterbody, river and physiographic-location clues.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s: Which one of the following statements about Vembanad is correct?
o: It is a brackish backwater in Kerala and the longest lake of India.
It is a saline lake in Rajasthan.
It is a meteorite-impact crater lake in Maharashtra.
It is a freshwater lake in Manipur with phumdis.
37.x: Vembanad is a brackish backwater in Kerala and is described as India's longest lake.
37.tq: Identify the lake from its distinctive type and ranking.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Srirangam — Island between the Kaveri and Kollidam
2. Aliabet — Largest island in the Narmada
3. Shivanasamudram — Riverine island associated with the Kaveri
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Srirangam lies between the Kaveri and Kollidam, Aliabet is the largest island in the Narmada, and Shivanasamudram is a Kaveri riverine island.
37.tq: Match each island with its river setting.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: Charaichung at Majuli, established in 1633 by Ahom king Pratap Singha, is associated with which description?
o: The first hydropower project on the Brahmaputra
The largest artificial lake of Assam
37.x: Charaichung was established in 1633 by Pratap Singha and is called Asia's first protected bird site.
37.tq: Recall the founder–date–designation association.
37.sec: Lakes and lagoons → state and type

37.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Himalayan rivers from Peninsular rivers?
o: Himalayan rivers form only estuaries, whereas Peninsular rivers form only deltas.
Himalayan rivers are seasonal, whereas Peninsular rivers are perennial.
Himalayan rivers generally have deep antecedent gorges, whereas Peninsular rivers have broad or shallow graded valleys.
Himalayan rivers have fixed straight courses, whereas Peninsular rivers meander extensively.
37.x: Himalayan rivers are generally perennial and form deep antecedent gorges, while Peninsular rivers are usually seasonal and flow through broad, shallow, graded valleys.
37.tq: Compare the two river systems feature by feature.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Himalayan rivers are generally perennial because they receive water from rainfall and snowmelt.
2. Peninsular rivers are mainly seasonal and rain-fed.
3. Peninsular rivers commonly have fixed and relatively straight courses over hard rock.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: All three statements correctly describe the regime and course characteristics of Himalayan and Peninsular rivers.
37.tq: Test the river-system comparison through separate regime and course statements.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the mouths of Peninsular rivers is correct?
o: All Peninsular rivers form large deltas.
Peninsular rivers do not form either deltas or estuaries.
West-flowing rivers always form larger deltas than east-flowing rivers.
East-flowing Peninsular rivers generally form deltas, while west-flowing rivers commonly form estuaries.
37.x: East-flowing Peninsular rivers generally form deltas, whereas west-flowing rivers commonly form estuaries.
37.tq: Use the east-flowing versus west-flowing contrast.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: Which of the following is an important use more characteristic of Peninsular rivers than Himalayan rivers?
o: Formation of antecedent valleys in the Himalaya
Navigation through perennial deep gorges only
37.x: Peninsular rivers are particularly useful for hydropower generation, while east-flowing rivers also support delta irrigation.
37.tq: Apply the functional comparison between the two river systems.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s:
Antecedent rivers are those which:
1. Rise in the Trans-Himalaya.
2. Maintain their courses by cutting gorges as mountain ranges rise.
3. Are represented by the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Antecedent rivers rise in the Trans-Himalaya and retain their courses by cutting through rising ranges. Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra are examples.
37.tq: Test definition, process and examples together.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: The Godavari delta, known as Konaseema, is described as having how many distributaries in the material?
37.x: The Godavari delta at Konaseema is described as having seven distributaries.
37.tq: Directly recall the numerical detail attached to the delta.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: Which of the following is NOT a distributary of the Godavari listed in connection with the Konaseema delta?
37.x: The listed Godavari distributaries include Gautami, Vasishta, Vainateya, Tulya, Bharadwaja, Kaushika and Athreya. Bhagirathi is not included in that list.
37.tq: Find the outsider from a named distributary list.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: The mouth of the Godavari is located near which place?
37.x: The Godavari reaches the sea near Antharvedi through its deltaic distributaries.
37.tq: Recall the terminal-location fact rather than the source.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: Which one of the following statements about the Ganga basin is correct?
o: The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna basin is India's smallest basin.
The Ganga is a seasonal Peninsular river.
The Ganga basin is smaller than the Narmada basin.
The Ganga alone covers approximately 9,51,600 sq km.
37.x: The Ganga alone covers approximately 9,51,600 sq km. The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna basin is the largest basin in India.
37.tq: Use the precise area figure to reject reversed basin claims.
37.sec: Peninsular vs Himalayan rivers

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Godavari — approximately 250 km in Andhra Pradesh
37.x: Approximately 250 km of the Godavari lies in Andhra Pradesh. The other length associations are incorrect.
37.tq: Use the state-specific length detail as the distinguishing clue.
37.sec: Basin area and length ranking

38.s: With reference to Andhi or pre-monsoon dust storms, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: They occur only during December and January.
They occur mainly from March to June.
They are gentle nocturnal winds of the coastal plains.
They are confined exclusively to Assam.
38.x: Andhi or dust storms are pre-monsoon phenomena occurring generally from March to June. They are associated mainly with Rajasthan and adjoining north-western regions.
38.tq: Reject extreme seasonal and regional restrictions in favour of the correct range.
38.sec: Hot-weather local storms and pre-monsoon showers → region  [APPSC]

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the hot season in India:
1. It generally extends from March to May.
2. Local convective storms during this period contribute about 10 per cent of the annual rainfall as pre-monsoon rain.
3. Pre-monsoon rain is useful for rice, jute, coffee, mango and tea.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The hot season generally lasts from March to May. Local convective storms produce about 10 per cent of annual rainfall as pre-monsoon rain, which benefits rice, jute, coffee, mango and tea.
38.tq: Test a season, a quantitative figure and its agricultural significance together.
38.sec: Hot-weather local storms and pre-monsoon showers → region  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following places recorded approximately 50°C during 1935 in the context of the hot season?
38.x: Ganganagar in Rajasthan recorded approximately 50°C in 1935, illustrating the intensity of the hot season in north-western India.
38.tq: Recall the location linked with a distinctive historical temperature record.
38.sec: Hot-weather local storms and pre-monsoon showers → region  [APPSC]

38.s: Dust aerosols over the Indo-Gangetic Plain assist the advance of the monsoon inland because they:
o: Reverse the direction of ocean currents
Heat the mid-troposphere and help pull the monsoon inland
Cool the lower troposphere and suppress convection
Eliminate pressure differences between land and sea
38.x: Dust aerosols heat the mid-troposphere over the Indo-Gangetic Plain. This heating helps pull the monsoon inland.
38.tq: Apply the stated cause-and-effect relationship rather than merely recalling a definition.
38.sec: Hot-weather local storms and pre-monsoon showers → region  [APPSC]

38.s: ‘Nautapa’ refers to:
o: A prolonged break in the northeast monsoon
A nine-day period of winter rainfall in south India
The first week of the southwest monsoon in Kerala
A nine-day period of peak summer heat in north India before the monsoon
38.x: Nautapa is the traditional nine-day peak of summer heat in north India and occurs just before the arrival of the monsoon.
38.tq: Identify a traditional climatic term by its duration, season and region.
38.sec: Hot-weather local storms and pre-monsoon showers → region  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the winds called monsoons?
o: Local winds confined to the coastal districts of India
Primary planetary winds that blow permanently in one direction
Upper-air winds that never reach the land surface
Seasonal or periodic secondary winds that reverse direction with the season
38.x: Monsoons are seasonal or periodic secondary winds. Their direction reverses with the change of season; they are not primary planetary winds.
38.tq: Distinguish monsoons from primary winds by their periodic reversal and classification.
38.sec: Monsoon characteristics - wind type, latitudinal limit, steadiness, distribution, breaks  [APPSC]

38.s: The monsoons are generally confined to the tropical belt between:
38.x: The monsoons are described as being confined to the tropics between 20°N and 20°S.
38.tq: Use the exact latitudinal limits rather than substituting the tropics’ astronomical boundaries.
38.sec: Monsoon characteristics - wind type, latitudinal limit, steadiness, distribution, breaks  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Indian monsoon?
o: Steady and uniform rainfall throughout the season
38.x: The Indian monsoon is not steady or uniformly distributed. Its important characteristics include seasonal reversal, unequal distribution, breaks and variability.
38.tq: Find the single reversed characteristic among otherwise correct monsoon features.
38.sec: Monsoon characteristics - wind type, latitudinal limit, steadiness, distribution, breaks  [APPSC]

38.s: The sudden onset of the south-west monsoon, generally noticed in the first week of June, is known as the:
38.x: The sudden onset of the south-west monsoon in the first week of June is called the monsoon burst.
38.tq: Match the climatic event with its standard technical term.
38.sec: Monsoon characteristics - wind type, latitudinal limit, steadiness, distribution, breaks  [APPSC]

38.s: Who noted the seasonal winds in the ninth century?
38.x: Al Masudi, a ninth-century scholar, noted the seasonal winds associated with the monsoon system.
38.tq: Identify the historical observer associated with the climatic phenomenon.
38.sec: Monsoon characteristics - wind type, latitudinal limit, steadiness, distribution, breaks  [APPSC]

38.s: The normal date of onset of the southwest monsoon over Kerala is:
38.x: The normal onset date of the southwest monsoon over Kerala is 1 June.
38.tq: Use the exact date rather than confusing onset over the islands, advance dates and countrywide coverage.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The southwest monsoon normally reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands approximately on:
38.x: The southwest monsoon reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands at about 25 May, before its normal onset over Kerala.
38.tq: Separate the earliest island onset from the normal mainland onset.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the duration of the southwest monsoon in India:
1. It lasts for less than 75 days in western Rajasthan.
2. It lasts for more than 120 days in the south-western peninsula.
3. Its duration is uniform throughout the country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The duration is less than 75 days in western Rajasthan and more than 120 days in the south-western peninsula. It is not uniform throughout India.
38.tq: Compare regional extremes and reject the absolute statement about uniformity.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: According to the revised normal dates of the India Meteorological Department, the southwest monsoon covers the whole country by:
38.x: The IMD's revised normal date for the southwest monsoon to cover the whole country is 8 July.
38.tq: Distinguish the revised date from approximate descriptions such as ‘by the end of June’ or ‘by the end of July’.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The India Meteorological Department fixes the onset of the southwest monsoon primarily by examining rainfall over:
38.x: The IMD uses rainfall recorded over five-day pentads while fixing the onset of the southwest monsoon.
38.tq: Identify the precise operational time unit instead of choosing a broader climatological period.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the approximate advance of the southwest monsoon?
o: Bhopal by 15 June and Delhi by 25 June
Bhopal by 25 May and Delhi by 1 June
Bhopal by 1 July and Delhi by 8 July
Bhopal by 25 June and Delhi by 15 July
38.x: The southwest monsoon normally reaches Bhopal around 15 June and Delhi around 25 June.
38.tq: Use the sequence and paired dates to distinguish advance dates from onset and withdrawal dates.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The southwest monsoon generally covers the country in approximately:
38.x: After its onset and advance, the southwest monsoon covers the country in about one month.
38.tq: Test the approximate duration of a process rather than a single station date.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s:
The IMD declaration of monsoon onset involves which of the following conditions after 10 May?
1. At least 60 per cent of 14 specified stations receive 2.5 mm of rain for two days.
2. Westerlies reach approximately the 600 hPa level.
3. The conditions are assessed only after the end of June.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: The onset criteria include rainfall of 2.5 mm for two days at 60 per cent of 14 stations and westerlies reaching about 600 hPa after 10 May. They are not assessed only after June.
38.tq: Find the false timing statement while retaining the precise threshold conditions.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: During a ‘break’ in the southwest monsoon, which one of the following conditions generally occurs?
o: The Arabian Sea branch reverses into a winter monsoon over the west coast.
The tropical easterly jet disappears and the westerly jet moves south of the Himalayas.
The monsoon trough shifts permanently to the Indian Ocean and all rainfall stops.
The monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, leaving the plains relatively dry.
38.x: During a monsoon break, the trough shifts towards the Himalayan foothills. The plains consequently experience dry conditions while the Himalayan region receives heavy rainfall.
38.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect relationship between trough position and regional rainfall.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from India normally:
o: Begins in the south in May and ends in August
Begins in the north-west in October and ends by the end of November
Begins in the east in September and ends by mid-October
Begins simultaneously throughout India in November
38.x: Withdrawal begins from north-western India in October and is generally complete by the end of November.
38.tq: Remember the direction and time span of withdrawal rather than the onset sequence.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bay of Bengal branch — moves north along the western coast after crossing the Western Ghats
Arabian Sea branch — Agumbe and Hulikal receive very heavy rainfall
Arabian Sea branch — first strikes the Meghalaya hills
Bay of Bengal branch — produces a rain-shadow region immediately east of the Western Ghats
38.x: Agumbe and Hulikal receive very heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch. The other descriptions interchange the paths and effects of the two branches.
38.tq: Use branch-specific routes and locations to eliminate swapped descriptions.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
o: It first reaches Myanmar and turns west along the Himalayan foothills.
It first affects the Western Ghats and the Malabar Coast, then moves north along the west coast.
It crosses the Himalayas and descends over the Ganga plains.
It originates over the Bay of Bengal and moves directly towards Meghalaya.
38.x: The Arabian Sea branch first strikes the Western Ghats and Malabar Coast and subsequently advances northward along the west coast.
38.tq: Trace the branch from its first landfall to its subsequent movement.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The rain-shadow region associated with the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon lies mainly:
o: To the west of the Malabar Coast
To the east of the Western Ghats
38.x: The Western Ghats force uplift on their windward side, leaving a rain-shadow region to their east.
38.tq: Use the windward-leeward comparison to identify the rain-shadow location.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The southwest monsoon season contributes approximately what proportion of India's annual rainfall?
38.x: The southwest monsoon season provides about 75 per cent of India's annual rainfall.
38.tq: Select the stated national share without confusing it with regional rainfall percentages.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The long-period average annual rainfall of India for 1971–2020 is given as:

38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s:
Which of the following phenomena are associated with the retreating southwest monsoon?
1. The Sun moves southward and the north-western low-pressure area weakens.
2. The westerly jet returns south of the Himalayas.
3. The tropical easterly jet disappears.
4. Clear skies and ‘October heat’ are experienced.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: All four conditions accompany the retreating monsoon. The weakening of the north-western low, jet-stream changes and clear, hot weather are characteristic of October–November.
38.tq: Test a complete cluster of associated seasonal characteristics.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: The bimodal rainfall received by parts of southern India during the retreating monsoon is mainly associated with:
o: The permanent high over the South Indian Ocean
38.x: Bay of Bengal cyclones bring bimodal rainfall to the south during the October–November retreating monsoon season.
38.tq: Match the seasonal rainfall feature with its immediate weather system.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following best describes monsoon winds?
o: Local winds confined to mountain valleys
Polar winds that move towards the equator in all seasons
Permanent winds blowing in one direction throughout the year
Seasonal winds that reverse direction between summer and winter
38.x: Monsoons are seasonal winds that reverse direction: they generally blow from sea to land in summer and from land to sea in winter.
38.tq: Use the defining seasonal reversal to distinguish monsoons from permanent and local winds.
38.sec: Onset and advance - first state, normal dates, the two branches  [APPSC]

38.s: According to the classical thermal theory of the monsoon, the summer monsoon is produced primarily because:
o: The ITCZ remains fixed south of the equator throughout the year.
Land heats faster than the sea, creating a low-pressure area over land that draws moist winds from the sea.
The Himalayas generate a cold high-pressure area over northern India in summer.
The sea heats faster than the land, creating a permanent low over the ocean.
38.x: Sir Edmund Halley's thermal theory, proposed in 1686, attributes the monsoon to differential heating of land and sea. Summer heating creates a low over land that attracts moist maritime winds.
38.tq: Apply the pressure-gradient logic of differential heating rather than memorising only the theory’s name.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: Who propounded the classical thermal theory of the monsoon in 1686?
38.x: Sir Edmund Halley propounded the classical thermal theory of the monsoon in 1686.
38.tq: Link the named theory with its associated scholar and year.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: The dynamic or ITCZ theory explains the southwest monsoon mainly through:
o: The cooling of the Tibetan Plateau during the summer months.
The northward shift of the ITCZ over the Ganga plain, drawing south-east trade winds across the equator as south-westerlies.
The southward shift of the ITCZ over the Indian Ocean during summer.
The permanent eastward movement of the subtropical westerly jet over peninsular India.
38.x: In summer, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Ganga plain as the monsoon trough. South-east trades cross the equator and are deflected to become south-westerly winds.
38.tq: Follow the movement of the pressure belt and the cross-equatorial wind path.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s:
Consider the following statements about jet streams and the Indian monsoon:
1. The subtropical westerly jet shifts north of the Himalayas during summer.
2. The tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea towards East Africa.
3. The return of the subtropical westerly jet south of the Himalayas is associated with monsoon withdrawal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All three statements are correct. The northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet is associated with onset, while its return south of the Himalayas accompanies withdrawal; the tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea to East Africa.
38.tq: Combine onset, withdrawal and jet-stream path statements before selecting the coded option.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: The heating of the Tibetan Plateau contributes to the southwest monsoon by:
o: Creating an upper-air anticyclone and strengthening the tropical easterly jet
Blocking all cross-equatorial winds in the Arabian Sea
Creating a permanent surface high and weakening the tropical easterly jet
Producing the subtropical westerly jet south of the Himalayas in summer
38.x: The Tibetan Plateau, at about 5,000 m, acts as a heat island in summer. Its intense heating produces an upper-air anticyclone and strengthens the tropical easterly jet.
38.tq: Connect plateau heating with its upper-air circulation effects.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the influence of ENSO on the Indian monsoon?
o: El Niño generally weakens the monsoon, whereas La Niña generally strengthens it.
El Niño always strengthens the monsoon, whereas La Niña weakens it.
ENSO has no relationship with monsoon variability.
Both El Niño and La Niña invariably weaken the monsoon.
38.x: El Niño generally weakens the Indian monsoon, while La Niña generally aids or strengthens it.
38.tq: Use the reversed-effect trap in paired climate phenomena.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: Which one of the following statements correctly represents the combined influence of IOD and MJO on the Indian monsoon?
o: An unfavourable MJO phase invariably produces a strong southwest monsoon.
A positive IOD can offset the adverse effect of El Niño, while an unfavourable MJO phase can stall the monsoon.
IOD affects only winter temperatures and MJO affects only Himalayan snowfall.
A positive IOD always eliminates El Niño, while every MJO phase strengthens rainfall.
38.x: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can partly offset the weakening influence of El Niño. An unfavourable phase of the Madden–Julian Oscillation can stall the monsoon.
38.tq: Separate the moderating role of IOD from the phase-dependent influence of MJO.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: The modern complex explanation of the Indian monsoon mechanism is dated in the material to:
38.x: The modern complex explanation of the monsoon mechanism is dated to 1957.
38.tq: Distinguish the modern explanatory framework from the date of the classical thermal theory.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: What would be the most significant climatic consequence for northern India if the Himalayas did not exist?
o: The southwest monsoon would reverse permanently into a north-easterly wind.
The region would receive heavier monsoon rainfall because cold air would enter freely.
Northern India would tend to become a desert because the Himalayas would no longer block cold Central Asian air or trap the monsoon.
The Tibetan Plateau would become a permanent oceanic low-pressure centre.
38.x: The Himalayas block cold Central Asian air and help trap the monsoon over the subcontinent. Without them, northern India would tend to become a desert.
38.tq: Apply the barrier and trapping functions of a major relief feature to a hypothetical situation.
38.sec: Monsoon mechanism theories - thermal, dynamic (ITCZ), jet stream, Tibet, ENSO/IOD  [APPSC]

38.s: Western disturbances affecting north-western India are best described as:
o: Mediterranean temperate cyclones reaching India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan
Tropical cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal
Local convectional storms originating over the Thar Desert
Retreating monsoon winds originating over the Arabian Sea
38.x: Western disturbances are temperate cyclones originating in the Mediterranean region and reaching north-western India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
38.tq: Identify the origin and pathway of the weather system.
38.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

38.s: Western disturbances are important for Indian agriculture mainly because they:
o: Produce rainfall on the Tamil Nadu coast during October
Bring heavy summer rain to the Deccan Plateau
Provide winter rainfall beneficial to rabi crops
Cause the onset of the south-west monsoon
38.x: Western disturbances bring about 10–15 cm of winter rain to north-western India, which is beneficial for rabi crops.
38.tq: Link a climatic phenomenon with its agricultural effect.
38.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

38.s: Which of the following regions receives snowfall due to western disturbances?
o: Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
Tamil Nadu, Kerala and coastal Karnataka
38.x: Western disturbances cause snowfall in the hills of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
38.tq: Match the weather system with its characteristic area.
38.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the retreating monsoon:

2. It is generally accompanied by clear skies.
3. It may produce cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The retreating monsoon occurs mainly in October-November, brings clear skies and is associated with cyclones from the Bay of Bengal.
38.tq: Test a cluster of characteristics through coded combinations.

o: A heat wave occurring exclusively in north-western India in April
Extreme heat caused by western disturbances
Hot and humid weather during the retreat of the monsoon
Cold and dry weather after the winter monsoon

38.s: The relative dryness of the Tamil Nadu coast during the south-west monsoon is mainly due to:

Its location on the leeward side and the winds blowing parallel to the coast
Its location north of the Tropic of Cancer
The absence of the Bay of Bengal

38.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: North-west India during western disturbances — No winter precipitation
Tamil Nadu coast during south-west monsoon — Relatively dry
South India during retreating monsoon — Absence of cyclonic activity

38.tq: Find the correctly matched regional effect among reversed alternatives.
38.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

o: Amw — West coast south of Goa
BWhw — Most of the peninsula south of the Tropic of Cancer

A semi-arid steppe climate in north-western Gujarat, western Rajasthan and parts of Punjab
A monsoon climate with dry summer on the Coromandel coast
A hot desert climate in extreme western Rajasthan

39.s: Which condition defines El Niño in the context of the equatorial Pacific?
