43.tq: Match the soil with its parent material.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s:
Consider the following statements regarding alluvial soil:
1. It is the most widespread soil in India.
2. It is particularly associated with the Indo-Gangetic Plain, deltas and coastal areas.
3. It is generally suitable for irrigated farming.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil, covers the Indo-Gangetic Plain, deltas and coasts, and is well suited to irrigated farming.
43.tq: Check whether all three statements describe the same soil profile before selecting the complete combination.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: The approximate area and percentage share of alluvial soil in India are respectively:
43.x: Alluvial soil covers approximately 15 lakh square kilometres, constituting about 45.6% of India’s area in the classification given.
43.tq: Keep the area-share pair together and distinguish it from the corresponding black and red soil figures.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Khadar — older alluvium with lime nodules
Bhabar — belt of pebbly alluvial fans
Terai — dry upland above the flood plain
43.x: Bhabar is a belt formed by pebbly alluvial fans. Khadar is new alluvium, Bhangar is older alluvium with kankar, and Terai is a swampy lowland.
43.tq: Use the precise age and landform distinctions among the alluvial subdivisions.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s:
With reference to Khadar and Bhangar, consider the following statements:
1. Khadar is new alluvium found in flood plains.
2. Bhangar is older alluvium situated at a higher level.
3. Bhangar is associated with kankar or lime nodules.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: Khadar is new flood-plain alluvium, while Bhangar is older, higher-level alluvium containing kankar or lime nodules.
43.tq: Separate the two confusable alluvial terms by age, elevation and kankar content.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Black or regur soil is primarily derived from the weathering of:
43.x: Black soil develops mainly from the weathering of Deccan Trap basalt.
43.tq: Apply the parent-rock association: basalt indicates black soil.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s:
Which of the following features are associated with black soil?
1. Clay content generally exceeding 62 per cent
2. High moisture retention
3. Deep cracks during summer
4. Self-ploughing character
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Black soil has more than 62% clay, retains moisture well, develops deep summer cracks and is known for its self-ploughing character.
43.tq: Group the characteristic traits of one soil rather than relying on a single keyword.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: The approximate area and percentage share of black soil are:
43.x: Black soil covers about 5.47 lakh square kilometres, or approximately 16.6% of India’s area in the stated classification.
43.tq: Distinguish the black-soil figures from the larger alluvial and smaller arid-soil figures.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following groups contains only regions associated with black soil?
o: Kerala, coastal Odisha, Sundarbans and Tamil Nadu
Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and the Rann of Kutch
Western Ghats, Rajmahal Hills and North-Eastern states
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and northern Karnataka
43.x: Black soil is chiefly distributed in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, western Andhra Pradesh and northern Karnataka.
43.tq: Use regional clustering to distinguish black soil from laterite, peaty and saline soils.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: The red colour of red soil is mainly due to:
43.x: Iron oxide gives red soil its characteristic red colour; hydration may make it appear yellow.
43.tq: Identify the colour-producing compound rather than the soil’s parent rock.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Red and yellow soils are mainly formed from:
o: Crystalline igneous rocks such as granite and gneiss
River deposits in the Indo-Gangetic Plain
43.x: Red and yellow soils develop mainly from crystalline igneous rocks, especially granite and gneiss, under relatively low rainfall conditions.
43.tq: Link the soil type to its stated parent-rock group.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of red and yellow soil?
o: Waterlogging with very high organic matter
Black colour and neutral to alkaline reaction
Very high moisture retention and abundance of humus
Porous and light texture with low moisture retention
43.x: Red and yellow soils are generally porous and light, with low moisture retention. They are also poor in lime, humus and phosphoric acid.
43.tq: Contrast the physical and nutrient properties with those of black soil.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Laterite soil is formed under which combination of conditions?
o: Waterlogging and accumulation of organic matter in humid lowlands
Low rainfall and low temperature with deposition of salts
Heavy leaching, rainfall above 200 cm and high temperature
43.x: Laterite forms through intense leaching under heavy rainfall exceeding 200 cm and high temperature.
43.tq: Identify the soil from the environmental process rather than from its location.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following statements about laterite soil is correct?
o: It is generally fertile without manuring and is rich in nitrogen and phosphate
It is rich in iron and aluminium oxides and is generally acidic and infertile
It is formed mainly from river deposits and contains abundant kankar
It has the highest moisture retention among Indian soils
43.x: Laterite soil is rich in iron and aluminium oxides but is generally acidic and infertile. It is poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium and has excess iron oxide and potash.
43.tq: Watch for the nutrient reversal trap in statements about laterite.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s:
Which of the following crops are associated with laterite soil when adequate manure is supplied?
1. Tea
2. Coffee
3. Rubber
4. Cashew
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Laterite soil can support tea, coffee, rubber and cashew cultivation when adequately manured.
43.tq: Read the crop list as a complete set and test each item against the soil condition.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following soil types is correctly matched with its principal area of distribution?
o: Laterite — Western Ghats, Rajmahal Hills and North-Eastern states
Saline soil — upper Himalayan slopes above the tree line
Peaty soil — western Rajasthan and the Thar
Arid soil — Sundarbans and coastal Kerala
43.x: Laterite soil occurs in the Western Ghats, Rajmahal Hills and North-Eastern states, besides other regions including parts of Andhra Pradesh.
43.tq: Find the correctly matched region while rejecting swapped soil environments.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following statements regarding arid or desert soil is correct?
o: It is naturally rich in lime, humus and nitrogen
It is sandy, poor in nitrogen and humus, and improves with irrigation
It is waterlogged and rich in organic matter
It is formed by intense leaching under heavy rainfall
43.x: Arid soil is sandy, deficient in nitrogen and humus, and its agricultural productivity can improve with irrigation. Kankar commonly occurs at lower depths.
43.tq: Combine the soil’s texture, deficiencies and management response.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: The approximate area and percentage share of arid or desert soil are respectively:
43.x: Arid or desert soil covers approximately 1.42 lakh square kilometres, constituting about 4.12% of the area in the given classification.
43.tq: Distinguish the paired area and percentage from the figures for laterite and peaty soils.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s:
Saline and alkaline soils are locally known by which of the following names?
1. Reh
2. Kallar
3. Usar
4. Thur
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Reh, kallar, usar and thur are among the local names used for saline and alkaline soils; other names include rakar and chopan.
43.tq: Treat a named-list question as a completeness check for every listed term.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: The major causes of the formation of saline and alkaline soils include:
o: Deposition of fresh river silt during annual floods
Accumulation of forest humus on mountain slopes
Heavy leaching and high temperature removing all soluble salts
Over-irrigation and poor drainage causing salt build-up
43.x: Salt build-up, often associated with over-irrigation and poor drainage, produces saline and alkaline soils.
43.tq: Infer the soil process from the stated land-management conditions.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Peaty and marshy soils are formed mainly where:
o: Rainfall is very low and wind deposits sand
Heavy rainfall and high humidity keep the soil waterlogged and organic matter accumulates
Basalt undergoes weathering in the Deccan Plateau
River deposits are raised above the flood plain
43.x: Peaty soils develop in waterlogged, humid conditions where heavy rainfall and high humidity promote the accumulation of organic matter.
43.tq: Match the formation process with the moisture and organic-matter conditions.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following statements about peaty and marshy soils is NOT correct?
o: They may occur in coastal West Bengal, Kerala, Odisha and Tamil Nadu
They are rich in organic matter
They are associated with waterlogged conditions
They are generally suitable for all crops because waterlogging improves aeration
43.x: Peaty and marshy soils are generally unsuitable for cultivation because persistent waterlogging restricts aeration. They are found in several coastal and humid regions and are rich in organic matter.
43.tq: Look for the statement that reverses the effect of waterlogging on cultivation.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which one of the following best describes forest and mountain soils?
o: Deep black soils formed from basalt in the Deccan Trap
Sandy soils rich in nitrogen and humus in western Rajasthan
Humus-rich soils on slopes, generally poor in potash and phosphorus
Salt-crusted soils of the coastal deltas
43.x: Forest and mountain soils are humus-rich, occur on slopes and are generally poor in potash and phosphorus. Mountain meadow soils may occur above the tree line.
43.tq: Use the distinctive humus and nutrient combination to identify the soil.
43.sec: Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions

43.s: Which soil has the highest moisture-retention capacity among the soils listed?
43.x: Black soil has the highest moisture-retention capacity, owing largely to its high clay content. Its deep summer cracks also give it a self-ploughing character.
43.tq: Compare the defining physical property rather than the geographical distribution.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s: Which one of the following sets contains nutrients in which black soil is comparatively rich?
43.x: Black soil is comparatively rich in calcium, potassium and magnesium, but deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.
43.tq: Separate the rich and deficient nutrient groups instead of reversing them.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Black soil is generally neutral to alkaline.
2. Red soil is deficient in lime, humus and phosphoric acid.
3. Black soil is generally deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All three statements are correct. Black soil is neutral to alkaline and rich in calcium, potassium and magnesium but deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus; red soil is poor in lime, humus and phosphoric acid.
43.tq: Compare the nutrient and reaction properties of black and red soils statement by statement.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s: Which group consists only of soils generally described as acidic?
43.x: Laterite, peaty and forest soils are generally acidic. Black soil is usually neutral to alkaline, while saline and alkaline soils have a different reaction.
43.tq: Identify the common chemical reaction shared by the three soils.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s: Laterite is used as a building material chiefly because it:
o: Has high moisture retention and expands in water
Is composed entirely of river-borne sand
Can be cut into bricks that harden on exposure to air
Contains abundant organic matter and remains soft when dry
43.x: Laterite can be cut into bricks, which harden when exposed to air, making it useful as a building material.
43.tq: Apply the material property to the practical use described.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s: Which one of the following statements about the nutrient composition of laterite soil is correct?
o: It is deficient only in potassium and contains no iron compounds
It is rich in humus and phosphorus because it forms in waterlogged areas
It is rich in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium, but lacks iron oxide
It is poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium, but has excess iron oxide and potash
43.x: Laterite is poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium and contains excess iron oxide and potash. The claim that nitrogen is plentiful in Andhra Pradesh laterite is incorrect.
43.tq: Spot the precise nutrient reversal and retain the iron-oxide association.
43.sec: Soil properties compared - moisture retention, acidity, lime/nitrogen/humus deficiency, building-material use

43.s: Which one of the following correctly describes sheet erosion?
o: Subsurface removal of soil resulting in sinkholes
Formation of deep trenches by concentrated surface flow
Downslope movement of soil under gravity
Removal of a thin, uniform layer of topsoil by overland flow
43.x: Sheet erosion removes a thin top layer uniformly through overland flow. It is widespread and generally the least noticeable form of erosion.
43.tq: Use the process-based definition to distinguish closely related erosion types.
43.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

43.s:
Consider the following statements regarding erosion types:
1. Rill erosion produces small channels cut by running water.
2. Wind erosion involves deflation, saltation and surface creep.
3. Tunnel erosion is caused by subsurface removal and may create sinkholes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All three statements are correct. Rills are small water-cut channels, wind erosion involves the three stated movements, and tunnel erosion removes soil below the surface and can form sinkholes.
43.tq: Test several process definitions together and select the inclusive code only after checking each statement.
43.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

43.s:
Arrange the following stages of water erosion in the correct sequence:
A. Gully erosion
B. Splash erosion
C. Rill erosion
D. Sheet erosion
43.x: Water erosion generally progresses from splash to sheet, then rill and finally gully erosion.
43.tq: Use the progression from dispersed impact to increasingly concentrated flow.
43.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

43.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Parts of Australia and Africa — sheet erosion
43.x: Parts of Australia and Africa are associated with tunnel erosion, in which subsurface removal may create sinkholes, not sheet erosion.
43.tq: Find the regional example that does not correspond to the stated erosion process.
43.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

43.s: Which of the following represents the correct order of increasing soil loss generally associated with the main forms of water erosion?
43.x: The usual progression of increasing soil loss is splash, sheet, rill and gully erosion. Water is described as the most powerful erosion agent in this context.
43.tq: Arrange processes by increasing intensity and concentration rather than by their visual size.
43.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

43.s: Wind erosion is generally most severe under which combination of conditions?
o: Mulched soil, low wind speed and frequent light rain
Waterlogged soil, gentle winds and heavy forest cover
Bare, dry, fine-textured soil with strong and frequent winds
Dense vegetation, moist clayey soil and weak winds
43.x: Wind erosion is worst where soil is bare, dry and fine-textured and winds are strong and frequent.
43.tq: Combine the environmental conditions instead of identifying a single isolated factor.
43.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

43.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Conservation method)
 a. Contour ploughing
 b. Terracing
 c. Check dams
 d. Shelter belts

List-II (Function)
 i. Trap sediment and check gully growth
 ii. Tree rows that reduce wind speed
 iii. Ploughing along contour lines to slow runoff
 iv. Steps cut on steep slopes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Contour ploughing slows runoff along contour lines; terracing creates steps; check dams trap sediment and limit gully growth; shelter belts reduce wind speed.
43.tq: Start from the sure process-function pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s: Strip cropping primarily involves:
o: Planting only trees in long strips across a watershed
Constructing permanent dams across every field channel
Alternating erosion-resistant crop strips, such as grass, with row-crop strips
43.x: Strip cropping alternates strips of erosion-resistant crops, such as grass, with row crops to reduce wind- and water-induced erosion.
43.tq: Distinguish a field-layout method from structural and tree-based conservation measures.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s:
Consider the following statements about conservation agriculture:
1. It may involve minimum or zero tillage.
2. Crop residue is retained as soil cover.
3. Mulch helps stabilise the soil.
4. It necessarily requires complete removal of crop residues.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: Conservation agriculture uses minimum or zero tillage, retains crop residues and uses mulch for soil stability. Complete removal of residues is contrary to the practice.
43.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the central principle of the conservation method.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a national soil and watershed-related programme or initiative?
o: Soil Health Card — construction of coastal shelter belts only
Desert Development Programme — replacement of all agricultural land by forests
RKVY — classification of Himalayan landslides only
43.x: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme is associated with the watershed development approach. The other descriptions do not represent the stated programmes or initiative.
43.tq: Identify the genuine programme-function relationship and reject exaggerated or exclusive descriptions.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s: The Watershed Development Component of PMKSY was formed by merging IWMP during:
43.x: IWMP began in 2009–10 and was merged in 2015–16 into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY.
43.tq: Separate the programme’s starting year from the year of institutional merger.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s:
Which of the following are included in the watershed approach associated with the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY?
1. Ridge-area treatment
2. Drainage-line treatment
3. Soil and moisture conservation
4. Linking all perennial rivers of the country
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: The approach includes ridge-area treatment, drainage-line treatment, and soil and moisture conservation. Linking all perennial rivers is not one of the listed components.
43.tq: Separate actual watershed-treatment components from an unrelated large-scale water-transfer claim.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s: Biochar used in soil conservation is associated with which of the following effects?
o: Increased wind speed at the soil surface
Complete elimination of soil erosion without vegetation
Lower water-holding capacity and higher soil nitrous oxide emissions
Higher water-holding capacity and an approximately 30–50% reduction in soil N2O emissions
43.x: Biochar raises the soil’s water-holding capacity and is associated with a reduction of soil N2O emissions of about 30–50%.
43.tq: Use the paired positive effects and numerical range to identify the precise option.
43.sec: Soil conservation methods

43.s: Mining-led deforestation is particularly associated with land degradation in which group of States?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
43.x: Mining-led deforestation is associated with Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. The other groups represent different or unsupported patterns.
43.tq: Match the specific land-degradation cause with its regional concentration.
43.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

43.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mining-led deforestation — Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Overgrazing — Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
Over-irrigation — Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
Climate change — only Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
43.x: Climate change is a general additional driver of land degradation and is not confined only to Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. The other pairs correctly reflect the stated associations.
43.tq: Watch for the restrictive word “only” when testing a broad causal factor.
43.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

43.s: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India is produced by which organisation?
43.x: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas is produced by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre.
43.tq: Apply the ‘who produces this report or atlas?’ identification method.
43.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

43.s: Which statement correctly describes the finding on sustainable soil-management practices in the FAO 2026 assessment?
o: They were equally worsening and improving in 75 countries.
They were worsening in about 10% of assessments and improving in 58%.
They were worsening in 58% of assessments and improving in only about 10%.
They were improving in all assessments.
43.x: The assessment reported worsening sustainable practices in 58% of assessments and improvement in only about 10%.
43.tq: Distinguish the larger deterioration percentage from the much smaller improvement percentage.
43.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

43.s: Which factor generally has a greater influence on soil erosion than the total annual amount of rainfall?
o: Length of the frost season alone
43.x: Rainfall intensity matters more than total annual rainfall because intense bursts can exceed the soil’s infiltration capacity and generate runoff.
43.tq: Discriminate between rainfall intensity and total rainfall, the key conceptual pair.
43.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

43.s:
Consider the following statements about factors controlling erosion:
1. Slope gradient influences the rate of soil erosion.
2. Vegetation cover and land use influence erosion.
3. Soil type and texture influence erosion.
4. Total annual rainfall is always more important than rainfall intensity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: Slope, vegetation and land use, and soil type and texture are important factors. Statement 4 is false because rainfall intensity generally matters more than total annual rainfall.
43.tq: Identify the reversed comparison in the final statement after checking the valid controlling factors.
43.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

43.s: Very intense bursts of rainfall can make soil drier because they:
o: Always infiltrate completely and recharge the soil
Exceed infiltration capacity, causing runoff or evaporation instead of recharge
Convert all soil organic carbon directly into clay
Prevent surface water from moving downslope
43.x: When rainfall intensity exceeds infiltration capacity, water runs off or evaporates rather than recharging the soil. This drying effect can offset the benefit of greater annual rainfall.
43.tq: Apply the infiltration-excess mechanism to an observed rainfall scenario.
43.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

43.s: Which one of the following statements about erosion estimation is correct?
o: RUSLE is used exclusively for earthquake prediction, and ICAR has prepared mineral maps.
RUSLE predicts long-term water erosion on slopes, and ICAR has prepared national cover-management and slope-factor maps.
RUSLE predicts only wind erosion in deserts, and ICAR has prepared only rainfall maps.
RUSLE measures only annual temperature, and ICAR has prepared only forest-fire maps.
43.x: RUSLE is used to predict long-term water erosion on slopes. ICAR has prepared national cover-management (C) and slope (P-factor) maps for erosion estimation.
43.tq: Match the model and institutional mapping work with their precise purposes.
43.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

43.s: A 2026 study applied RUSLE together with GIS to study erosion in the hills of:
43.x: A 2026 study paired RUSLE with GIS for studying erosion in the hills of North-East India.
43.tq: Use the geographic application area to distinguish the study from unrelated physiographic regions.
43.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

43.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship between soil properties, slope and carbon?
o: Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, while steep slopes can lose carbon-rich topsoil.
Sandy soils always hold more soil organic carbon than clay soils, and steep slopes conserve topsoil.
Clay soils cannot retain soil organic carbon.
Slope has no relation to the loss of carbon-rich topsoil.
43.x: Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, whereas steep slopes are more prone to losing carbon-rich topsoil.
43.tq: Test the paired comparison between soil texture and slope-related carbon loss.
43.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

43.s: With reference to the distribution of black soils in the Deccan Plateau, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Very deep black soils are concentrated in the eastern Deccan Plateau and become deeper towards the south.
Black soils occur only along the coastal plains of the Deccan Plateau.
Very deep black soils occur in the north-western Deccan Plateau and become thinner towards the east and south.
Black soils are uniformly deep throughout the Deccan Plateau.
43.x: Very deep black soils are found in the north-western Deccan Plateau. They become medium, thin and shallow towards the east and south.
43.tq: Use the location and directional trend to distinguish the correct geographical statement.

43.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of crops associated with black soil cultivation?
o: Tea, coffee, rubber, coconut and arecanut
Rice, sugarcane, jute, tea and coconut
Cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco and oilseeds
Barley, apple, saffron, tea and rubber
43.x: Black soils, also called black cotton soils, are suited to cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco, oilseeds and wheat. They are also suitable for dry farming.
43.tq: Select the option containing only crops linked with the soil under consideration.
43.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

43.s:
Consider the following statements regarding black soils in Andhra Pradesh:
1. They occupy about one-fourth of the land area of the State.
2. Deep black soils occur at Adoni and Alur.
3. The Kunderu basin and parts of Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Kurnool contain black soils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All three statements are correct. Black soils cover about 25% of Andhra Pradesh, with deep black soils at Adoni and Alur and important areas in the Kunderu basin, Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Kurnool.
43.tq: Combine the area, location and distribution statements before selecting the coded option.
43.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

43.s:
Which of the following crops are specifically mentioned in relation to black soils of Andhra Pradesh?
1. Cotton
2. Maize
3. Chillies
4. Turmeric
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Cotton, maize, chillies and turmeric are all grown in the black-soil regions of Andhra Pradesh.
43.tq: Check the complete crop list rather than selecting only the best-known black-soil crop.
43.sec: Black soil depth variation across the Deccan and suited crops

43.s: Peaty and marshy soils are generally formed under which of the following conditions?
o: Moderate rainfall, steep slopes and rapid erosion
Heavy rainfall, high humidity, waterlogging and accumulation of organic matter
Arid climate, wind deposition and alkaline irrigation
Low rainfall, intense evaporation and deficient drainage
43.x: Peaty and marshy soils form in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity where waterlogging permits organic matter to accumulate.
43.tq: Match the soil type with its characteristic climatic and drainage conditions.
43.sec: Peaty/marshy soils - climatic conditions and areas

43.s: Which one of the following is NOT an area associated with peaty or marshy soils?
43.x: Peaty and marshy soils occur in Kerala, the Sundarbans, coastal Odisha and Tamil Nadu, north Bihar and Almora. Western Rajasthan is not listed among these areas.
43.tq: Find the geographically incongruous area among the listed soil regions.
43.sec: Peaty/marshy soils - climatic conditions and areas

43.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes peaty soils from saline soils?
o: Peaty soils form mainly due to excessive evaporation in deserts.
Peaty soils are associated with waterlogging and organic accumulation, whereas semi-arid conditions with salinity describe saline soils.
Peaty soils are formed only in semi-arid regions with salinity.
Peaty soils are always alkaline and contain no organic matter.
43.x: Peaty soils are black, heavy and highly acidic, forming under waterlogged, humid conditions. Semi-arid climate with salinity is characteristic of saline soils, not peaty soils.

43.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Alkaline soil — lime as the principal amendment
Acidic soil — salt-tolerant crops as the sole reclamation measure
43.x: Gypsum is used to reclaim alkaline or sodic soils, while lime is used for acidic soils. Drainage, leaching and salt-tolerant crops can also assist reclamation.
43.tq: Start with the sure amendment-soil pair and eliminate the reversed combinations.
43.sec: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

43.s: Karewa soils are best described as:
o: Wind-deposited sandy soils of western Rajasthan
Lacustrine deposits forming plateaus above the Jhelum plains in the Kashmir Valley
Black cotton soils formed over basalt in the Deccan
Recent alluvial deposits of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
43.x: Karewas are old lake-bed deposits of unconsolidated gravel and mud. They form plateau-like surfaces above the Jhelum plains in the Kashmir Valley and are also found in the Bhadarwah valley.
43.tq: Use the origin and landform description to identify the correct soil type.
43.sec: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

43.s: Karewa soils are particularly famous for the cultivation of:
43.x: Karewas are famous for saffron cultivation around Pampore. Almonds and walnuts are also associated with them, and high-density apple planting is expanding on these deposits.
43.tq: Identify the signature crop associated with a distinctive regional soil.
43.sec: Problem soils - saline and alkaline soil reclamation (gypsum, lime), Karewa soils and their crop

43.s:
Which of the following statements regarding land degradation is/are correct?
1. Salinity can hinder water and nutrient uptake by plants.
2. Salinity can break up soil structure and pollute water bodies.
3. Alkalinity may result from limestone or basalt parent material and alkaline irrigation water.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Salinity affects plant water and nutrient uptake, damages soil structure and may pollute water bodies. Alkalinity can be associated with limestone or basalt parent material and alkaline irrigation water.

43.s: The major cause of salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging in irrigated areas is:
o: Scientific irrigation combined with adequate drainage
Excessive crop rotation and contour farming
43.x: Unscientific irrigation practices combined with inadequate drainage promote salinity, alkalinity and waterlogging.
43.tq: Identify the cause-effect relationship rather than a reclamation measure.
43.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

43.s: Without adequate preservation measures, what proportion of the world's arable land could be affected by 2050 according to the stated projection?
43.x: The stated projection is that 50% of the world's arable land could be affected by 2050 if soil resources are not preserved.

43.s: Which one of the following groups contains the states identified as affected by salinity and alkalinity problems?
o: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Assam and Sikkim
Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya, Nagaland and Manipur
43.x: The affected states listed are Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Canal-irrigated Punjab experienced salinity and alkalinity after the Green Revolution.
43.tq: Use the complete regional grouping to avoid substituting neighbouring states.
43.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

43.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate combination for reclaiming alkaline soil and curing waterlogging, respectively?
o: Organic litter alone and increased irrigation
Salt addition and land raising without drains
43.x: Gypsum is used with water management to reclaim alkaline soil. Waterlogging is addressed through drains, land levelling and tolerant crop varieties.
43.tq: Match each problem with its specific reclamation measure instead of reversing the remedies.
43.sec: Land degradation - salinity, alkalinity, waterlogging - causes, affected states, reclaiming agents

43.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five classical factors of soil formation?
43.x: The five classical factors are parent material, climate, relief or topography, organisms and time. Latitude is not included in this five-factor list.
43.tq: Recall the standard five-factor framework and identify the extra term.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about soil formation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Climate, altitude and bedrock influence soil formation.
2. Andhra Pradesh soils are mainly a mixture of sand, silt and clay.
3. Silt deposited by the Godavari, Krishna and Pennar contributes to soil formation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh soil formation reflects climate, altitude, bedrock and river deposits, while its soils mainly comprise sand, silt and clay.
43.tq: Combine general soil-forming factors with the State-specific examples.
43.sec: Soil formation factors - parent rock, climate, relief, organisms, time

43.s: Which one of the following represents the approximate volume composition of a good soil?
o: Mineral matter 45%, organic matter 5%, water 25%, air 25%
Mineral matter 50%, organic matter 25%, water 15%, air 10%
Mineral matter 25%, organic matter 45%, water 25%, air 5%
Mineral matter 5%, organic matter 45%, water 25%, air 25%
43.x: A good soil is approximately composed of 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water and 25% air by volume.
43.tq: Check that all four components and their percentages are correctly paired.

43.s: Which one of the following statements about soil organic carbon is correct?
o: It binds soil particles into aggregates, raises infiltration and feeds microbes.
It reduces the water-holding capacity of clay soils in all conditions.
It disperses soil particles and reduces microbial activity.
It occurs mainly in sandy subsoil and is absent from topsoil.
43.x: Soil organic carbon binds particles into aggregates, improves infiltration and supports microbial activity. Clay soils hold more organic carbon than sandy soils, and topsoil holds the most.
43.tq: Choose the option describing the functions of the soil component rather than an opposite effect.

43.s: India's average soil organic carbon reportedly declined over a period of 70 years from:
43.x: The reported decline in India's average soil organic carbon was from 1% to 0.3% over 70 years.
43.tq: Watch for reversal of the initial and final values in the percentage pair.
43.sec: Soil composition - components for plant growth, organic matter and water holding

43.s: Which one of the following soil orders occupies the largest share of India's area in the ICAR/USDA classification?
43.x: Inceptisols are the largest soil order in the stated classification, covering approximately 39.7% of India's area.
43.tq: Identify the largest category from the comparative area distribution.

43.s:
Arrange the following soil orders in descending order of their share of India's area:
A. Alfisols
B. Entisols
C. Inceptisols
D. Vertisols

43.tq: Arrange the categories by comparing their numerical shares from highest to lowest.

43.x: Aridisols account for approximately 4.3% of India's area. Ultisols account for about 2.5%, Mollisols 0.4% and Vertisols 8.5%.

43.tq: Compare the lower end of the distribution rather than the largest categories.

6. R — bedrock

43.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Soil Health Card generation and testing is correct?

A ₹92 crore programme involving 62,200 quintals of sunn hemp and wheat seed
A ₹62.20 lakh programme involving 91,918 quintals of groundnut and maize seed
A ₹26.20 crore programme involving 19,918 quintals of paddy and cotton seed

44.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes major and minor minerals under the MMDR framework?

Both major and minor minerals are regulated exclusively by the Centre.

the wettest place, with rainfall above 200 cm

Arrange the following seasons of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order of their usual periods, beginning with the earliest:

Deltaic — Anantapur, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa
Semi-arid Rayalaseema — Araku, Lambasingi and Horsley Hills
Hill or micro-climate — Krishna, Konaseema and Godavari districts

o: It includes Anantapur and YSR Kadapa, with frequent drought and very low rainfall.
It includes Srikakulam and Kakinada, with the highest rainfall in the Sileru valley.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the climate regions of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The semi-arid Rayalaseema region includes Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kurnool, Nandyal and YSR Kadapa.

Rainfall is highest in the Hagari valley and increases towards Rayalaseema.

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

the principal rainy season, with temperatures above 47°C

only tropical cyclones from the Arabian Sea

o: Northern America, Latin America and Europe are among the most urbanised continents or regions.
Africa has the highest current level of urbanisation and the slowest urban growth.
Asia has no significant urban growth.
Urbanisation is concentrated entirely in Europe.
56.x: Northern America, Latin America and Europe are among the most urbanised regions, whereas Africa and Asia are experiencing the fastest urban growth.
56.tq: Distinguish the level of urbanisation from the speed of urban growth.
56.sec: World urbanisation patterns

56.s: According to the older UN DESA series, approximately what share of the world's population lived in urban areas?
56.x: The older UN DESA series placed the urban share of the world population at about 55 per cent.
56.tq: Identify the figure associated with the specified statistical series.
56.sec: World urbanisation patterns

56.s: Under the WUP 2025 method, cities account for approximately what share of the world's population of about 8.2 billion?
56.x: The WUP 2025 method estimates that cities contain about 45 per cent of the world's approximately 8.2 billion people.
56.tq: Avoid confusing the revised urban definition with the older UN DESA estimate.
56.sec: World urbanisation patterns

56.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the largest cities identified under the WUP 2025 data?
56.x: Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi are identified among the largest cities; Cairo is not included in that listed group.
56.tq: Find the outsider in a specified urban hierarchy rather than relying on general city size knowledge.
56.sec: World urbanisation patterns

56.s: Over-urbanisation is most directly associated with a situation in which:
o: Rural population grows faster than urban population
Urban growth is faster than the availability of urban jobs and services
Urban growth is slower than the expansion of urban employment and services
56.x: Over-urbanisation occurs when urban population growth outpaces jobs and services, often resulting in slums.
56.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect relationship to an urban development scenario.
56.sec: World urbanisation patterns

56.s: According to the UN-Habitat World Cities Report 2026, approximately how many people live in slums or informal settlements?
56.x: The report estimates that about 1.1 billion people live in slums or informal settlements.
56.tq: Recall the order of magnitude of a current urbanisation statistic.
56.sec: World urbanisation patterns

56.s: Which group of countries is associated with low birth rates, ageing and population decline?
56.x: Italy, Japan and South Korea are noted for low birth rates, ageing populations and demographic decline.
56.tq: Use a country-group association rather than treating ageing as a universal regional feature.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly associated with Stage 5 of the demographic transition model?
56.x: Japan and Germany are examples of Stage 5, characterised by very low birth rates, low death rates and declining population.
56.tq: Match the illustrative countries to the correct transition stage.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s: Which one of the following countries is NOT included among the countries specifically identified as having shrinking populations?
56.x: Japan, China and several European countries are experiencing population decline; Nigeria is not included in that group.
56.tq: Use the demographic trend to eliminate the country with a contrasting population pattern.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s:
Consider the following statements regarding total fertility rates:
1. The total fertility rate of the USA is 1.6.
2. Finland has a lower total fertility rate than Japan.
3. The world average total fertility rate is 2.2.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: The USA has a TFR of 1.6 and the world average is 2.2. Finland's TFR is 1.4, which is lower than Japan's 1.3 statement is false because 1.4 is higher than 1.3.
56.tq: Check the direction of a comparison instead of merely recognising both figures.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's projected elderly population and median age in 2051?
56.x: India's elderly population is projected to reach 325.3 million and the median age to rise to 40 years by 2051.
56.tq: Keep population size and median-age projections paired with the correct year.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s: Which State had the highest elderly share according to SRS 2024?
56.x: Kerala had the highest elderly share at 15 per cent, while Assam had the lowest among the stated figures at 7.6 per cent.
56.tq: Identify the extreme value in a state-wise comparison.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s: The share of persons aged 65 years and above in the Asia-Pacific region is projected to reach what level by 2050?
56.x: The 65-plus population share in Asia-Pacific is projected to reach 18.6 per cent by 2050.
56.tq: Recall the projected age-specific percentage and its target year.
56.sec: Ageing populations - ageing/shrinking countries, median age

56.s: Which continent is projected to have the fastest population growth?
56.x: Africa is identified as the fastest-growing continent in population terms.
56.tq: Distinguish the fastest-growing continent from the largest-population continent.
56.sec: Regional growth and projections - fastest regions, UN projections, sex ratio

56.s: According to the UN World Population Prospects 2022, the projected world population in 2050 is:
56.x: The UN projected 8.5 billion in 2030, 9.7 billion in 2050 and 10.4 billion in 2100.
56.tq: Select the projection corresponding to the specified year rather than the neighbouring milestone.
56.sec: Regional growth and projections - fastest regions, UN projections, sex ratio

56.s: The strongly male-skewed sex ratios of Gulf States are primarily associated with:
56.x: Large inflows of male migrant workers produce highly male-skewed sex ratios in Gulf States.
56.tq: Link a demographic pattern to its principal migration-related cause.
56.sec: Regional growth and projections - fastest regions, UN projections, sex ratio

56.s: Which of the following correctly states the working-age population shares of the UAE and Qatar?
o: UAE 65.7 per cent and Qatar 65.6 per cent
UAE 75.7 per cent and Qatar 75.6 per cent
UAE 95.7 per cent and Qatar 95.6 per cent
UAE 85.7 per cent and Qatar 85.6 per cent
56.x: The working-age shares were 85.7 per cent in the UAE and 85.6 per cent in Qatar, among the world's highest.
56.tq: Distinguish closely spaced percentage figures by retaining their country order.
56.sec: Regional growth and projections - fastest regions, UN projections, sex ratio

56.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Stage 2 of the demographic transition model?
o: High birth rate, falling death rate and population explosion — India, 1951–81
Low birth rate, low death rate and stable population — India, 1951–81
Very low birth rate, low death rate and declining population — India overall now
Falling birth rate, low death rate and slowing growth — pre-industrial society
56.x: Stage 2 is characterised by high but declining death rates, high birth rates and population explosion; India during 1951–81 is an example.
56.tq: Match the stage by checking all three elements: rates, growth pattern and example.
56.sec: Demographic transition model - stages and countries

56.s:
Arrange the following stages of the demographic transition model in the correct order:
A. Low birth rate and low death rate with stable population
B. High birth rate and high death rate with low growth
C. Very low birth rate and low death rate with declining population
D. High birth rate and falling death rate with population explosion
56.x: The sequence is Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 4 and Stage 5: B, D, A, C.
56.tq: Identify the progression from pre-industrial conditions to population decline.
56.sec: Demographic transition model - stages and countries

56.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the demographic transition stage indicated in the material?
56.x: India overall is placed in Stage 3, characterised by falling birth rates, low death rates and slowing growth. Andhra Pradesh is cited as a Stage 4 example, while Japan and Germany are in Stage 5.
56.tq: Use the country or region example to reject stage substitutions.
56.sec: Demographic transition model - stages and countries

56.s: Total fertility rate refers to the average number of children born to a woman during which age span?
56.x: Total fertility rate is the average number of children per woman over the reproductive age span of 15–49 years.
56.tq: Recall the official age span in the definition rather than a general reproductive-age range.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: The replacement-level total fertility rate is generally taken as:
56.x: A total fertility rate of 2.1 is conventionally regarded as the replacement level.
56.tq: Distinguish the replacement benchmark from current national fertility values.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s:
Consider the following statements about SRS 2024 fertility estimates:
1. India's total fertility rate was 1.9.
2. Rural total fertility rate was 2.1, while urban total fertility rate was 1.5.
3. Delhi recorded the highest total fertility rate at 2.9.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: India's TFR was 1.9, with rural and urban values of 2.1 and 1.5 respectively. Delhi recorded the lowest TFR at 1.2, not the highest.
56.tq: Find the reversed extreme-value statement in a statistical comparison.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: According to SRS 2024, India's total fertility rate remained below replacement level for the:
56.x: India's TFR was below 2.1 for the fifth consecutive year in SRS 2024.
56.tq: Recall the duration attached to a current demographic trend.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the SRS 2024 total fertility rate?
56.x: Bihar had the highest stated TFR at 2.9; Uttar Pradesh had 2.6, Madhya Pradesh 2.4 and Delhi the lowest at 1.2.
56.tq: Start with the highest-value state and check the remaining state-value associations.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: Which group of States had a total fertility rate of 1.3 according to the stated SRS 2024 figures?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
Tamil Nadu, Bihar and West Bengal
56.x: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal each had a stated TFR of 1.3.
56.tq: Identify the complete matching group rather than one isolated state.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the NFHS-6 total fertility rate findings for 2023–24?
o: India's TFR was 2.0; urban TFR was 1.6; 31 of 36 States/UTs were below 2.1.
India's TFR was 1.5; urban TFR was 2.0; 6 of 36 States/UTs were below 2.1.
India's TFR was 2.7; urban TFR was 2.1; 31 of 36 States/UTs were above 2.1.
India's TFR was 1.9; urban TFR was 1.5; all States/UTs were below 2.1.
56.x: NFHS-6 reported an overall TFR of 2.0, an urban TFR of 1.6, and 31 of 36 States/UTs below the replacement level.
56.tq: Use the precise multi-part option and reject altered figures or reversed proportions.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the States/Union Territories with the lowest and highest NFHS-6 total fertility rates respectively?
o: Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Bihar
Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Madhya Pradesh
56.x: Andaman and Nicobar Islands recorded the lowest TFR at 0.9, while Bihar recorded the highest at 2.7 in NFHS-6.
56.tq: Compare the two extremes and preserve the order asked in the question.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the total fertility rate reported in the specified source or year?
56.x: India's TFR was reported as 1.9 in the 2023 SRS figures. The earlier 2010 figure was 2.5, NFHS-6 reported 2.0, and Andhra Pradesh's TFR was 1.5.
56.tq: Separate similar fertility figures by checking both the source and the year.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: The total fertility rate of Andhra Pradesh, according to the cited AP Survey 2025–26 analysis based on SRS 2023, was:
56.x: Andhra Pradesh's total fertility rate was reported as 1.5 in the cited analysis.
56.tq: Directly recall the State-specific demographic indicator without substituting the national value.
56.sec: Total fertility rate and replacement level

56.s: The dependency ratio is calculated as the ratio of which of the following?
o: Population aged 15–64 years to the population aged 65 years and above
Population aged 0–14 years and 65 years and above to the working-age population
Working-age population to the total population aged 0–14 years
Total non-working population to the total population below 14 years
56.x: The dependency ratio compares dependants—those aged 0–14 years and 65 years or above—with the working-age population.
56.tq: Use the exact age groups and denominator to distinguish the demographic indicator.
56.sec: Dependency ratio - young vs old

56.s: A decline in the dependency ratio, other conditions remaining favourable, is generally associated with which of the following demographic possibilities?
o: A reduction in the proportion of the working-age population
An immediate increase in the old-age population only
56.x: A lower dependency ratio means that relatively fewer dependants are supported by the working-age population, creating a potential demographic dividend.
56.tq: Apply the relationship between the dependency burden and the demographic dividend.
56.sec: Dependency ratio - young vs old

56.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, which one of the following is identified as a likely consequence of the dependency ratio doubling?
o: The disappearance of the working-age population
A complete decline in demand for healthcare services
Geriatric care becoming a growth job sector
A permanent fall in the elderly population
56.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 cautions that a doubling of the dependency ratio will increase the importance of geriatric care as a growth-oriented employment sector.
56.tq: Link the projected demographic trend with its sectoral employment implication.
56.sec: Dependency ratio - young vs old

56.s:
With reference to Tamil Nadu’s old-age dependency ratio, consider the following statements:
1. It was 20.6 in 2021.
2. It is projected to rise to 32.7 by 2036.
3. The projected change indicates a decline in the old-age dependency burden.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: Tamil Nadu’s old-age dependency ratio was 20.6 in 2021 and is projected to reach 32.7 by 2036. Statement 3 is false because the increase represents a rising, not declining, old-age dependency burden.
56.tq: Find the incorrect statement by checking the direction of change in the numerical trend.
56.sec: Dependency ratio - young vs old

56.s: The median age of Tamil Nadu was reported as which of the following?
56.x: Tamil Nadu’s median age was reported as 34.25 years.
56.tq: Distinguish the exact demographic figure from nearby numerical distractors.
56.sec: Dependency ratio - young vs old

56.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent total fertility rate estimates:
1. The SRS 2024 reported a total fertility rate of 1.9.
2. NFHS-6 reported a total fertility rate of 2.0.
3. Both figures were cited in the context of May–June 2026 demographic developments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
56.x: The SRS 2024 TFR was cited as 1.9 and the NFHS-6 TFR as 2.0; both figures were discussed in the May–June 2026 context.
56.tq: Verify each statement independently when several recent numerical facts are combined.
56.sec: Universal angles

56.s: The Andhra Pradesh Draft Population Management Policy, dated 5 March 2026, proposes to raise the total fertility rate from which level to which target?
56.x: The policy proposes raising Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate from 1.5 to 2.1.
56.tq: Match the policy with its precise baseline and target figures.
56.sec: Universal angles

56.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Draft Population Management Policy, the proposed incentive for a third child and a fourth child, respectively, is:
56.x: The proposed incentive is Rs 30,000 for a third child and Rs 40,000 for a fourth child.
56.tq: Use the order of the child number and the corresponding amount to avoid a swapped-pair trap.
56.sec: Universal angles

56.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the demographic and policy position of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Andhra Pradesh is in DTM stage 5 and is replacing fertility incentives with migration controls.
Andhra Pradesh is in DTM stage 3 and is retaining an exclusive population-control approach.
Andhra Pradesh is in DTM stage 4 and the policy approach is shifting from population control to “Pillale Sampada”.
Andhra Pradesh is in DTM stage 2 and is shifting from population promotion to population control.
56.x: Andhra Pradesh is identified as being in DTM stage 4, with the policy emphasis shifting from population control to “Pillale Sampada”, meaning children are wealth.
56.tq: Discriminate between adjacent demographic-transition stages and contrasting policy approaches.
56.sec: Universal angles

56.s: Which of the following best expresses the significance of the demographic dividend window for India?
o: It has already closed because the dependency ratio is rising in every State.
It closes after 2041, making skilling and employment generation time-bound priorities.
It closes in 2031, after which only fertility reduction is required.
It will remain open indefinitely because the working-age population always increases.
56.x: The demographic dividend window is expected to close after 2041; therefore, skilling and creation of suitable jobs are time-bound priorities.
56.tq: Identify the precise deadline and connect it with the stated policy priorities.
56.sec: Universal angles

57.s: Density of population is expressed as:
o: Number of persons per unit area
Annual population growth per square kilometre
57.x: Population density is the number of persons living per unit area, generally expressed per square kilometre. It is a crude measure of the man-land relationship.
57.tq: Use the exact definition rather than a related demographic measure.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the final 2011 population-density figures for the three major States?
57.x: The final 2011 figures are 1,106 persons per square kilometre for Bihar, 1,028 for West Bengal and 860 for Kerala. The other combinations mix provisional and final values or interchange States.
57.tq: Distinguish final census figures from nearby provisional figures.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to population density in 2011?
o: Arunachal Pradesh—17 persons per sq km
Andaman and Nicobar Islands—17 persons per sq km
57.x: Among the bigger States, Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density at 17 persons per square kilometre. Mizoram had 52, Sikkim 86 and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands 46.
57.tq: Start from the sure State–figure pair and reject swapped values.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NCT of Delhi — 11,320 persons per sq km
2. Chandigarh — 9,258 persons per sq km
3. Puducherry — 2,598 persons per sq km
4. Andaman and Nicobar Islands — 46 persons per sq km
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
57.x: All four pairs are correct for the 2011 figures given: Delhi 11,320, Chandigarh 9,258, Puducherry 2,598 and Andaman and Nicobar Islands 46 persons per square kilometre.
57.tq: Check each numerical pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: Among the southern States, which one had the highest population density in 2011?
57.x: Kerala had the highest population density among the southern States, at 860 persons per square kilometre. Andhra Pradesh had a density of 304.
57.tq: Use regional comparison rather than the national ranking alone.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: Which of the following statements regarding the density of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Its density was 304 persons per square kilometre.
Its density was below 100 persons per square kilometre.
It had the highest density among southern States.
Its density was 860 persons per square kilometre.
57.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a population density of 304 persons per square kilometre. Kerala, not Andhra Pradesh, had the highest density among southern States.
57.tq: Avoid the regional leader trap by separating State-specific and comparative figures.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: On the 13-district Census base, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest population density?
57.x: Krishna district had the highest density on the 13-district Census base, with 518 persons per square kilometre. YSR Kadapa and Prakasam had densities below 200 on that base.
57.tq: Read the administrative-base qualifier carefully before choosing the district.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: With reference to the 28-district map of Andhra Pradesh, which pair is correctly matched?
57.x: On the 28-district map, Visakhapatnam had the highest density at 1,870 persons per square kilometre, while Polavaram had the lowest at 54.
57.tq: Use the map-base distinction to avoid confusing the two sets of district figures.
57.sec: Density - definition, national figure, densest/sparsest states, UTs, districts  [APPSC]

57.s: Which of the following statements about BIMARU is correct?
o: It refers to Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, traditionally identified with development lag.
It refers to Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, identified with high industrialisation.
It denotes all States having a population density below the national average.
It is an official constitutional classification of economically backward States.
57.x: BIMARU is formed from Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The term described their historically poor socio-economic and development indicators and is not an official constitutional category.
57.tq: Separate a descriptive acronym from an official administrative classification.
57.sec: BIMARU states - term, coiner, profile  [APPSC]

57.s:
Consider the following statements about the BIMARU States:
1. They have historically lagged in several development indicators.
2. They are presently described as youthful States with high fertility.
3. Bihar has the highest total fertility rate among them as stated in the cited demographic profile.
4. Their growth has no connection with the delimitation debate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Their faster population growth is connected with the delimitation debate, so statement 4 is false.
57.tq: Identify the statement that uses an absolute negative to contradict a stated relationship.
57.sec: BIMARU states - term, coiner, profile  [APPSC]

57.s: Which one of the following demographic profiles is associated with the BIMARU States?
o: Low fertility and a narrow demographic-dividend window
High fertility and a comparatively wide demographic-dividend window
Population decline caused mainly by emigration
Ageing population with no growth advantage
57.x: The BIMARU States are described as youthful States with high fertility and a wide window for demographic dividend. Bihar’s crude birth rate was cited as 26.8.
57.tq: Match the regional label with its demographic profile, not merely its historical meaning.
57.sec: BIMARU states - term, coiner, profile  [APPSC]

57.s: Which of the following States recorded the highest share of India’s population in 2011?
57.x: Uttar Pradesh ranked first, accounting for 16.49 per cent of India’s population in 2011. Maharashtra, Bihar and West Bengal followed it in the listed order.
57.tq: Compare percentage shares rather than relying on area or density.
57.sec: State-wise population and area ranking  [other exams]

57.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of their share of India’s population in 2011:
A. Bihar
B. Uttar Pradesh
C. Andhra Pradesh (undivided)
D. Maharashtra
57.x: The correct order is Uttar Pradesh (16.49%), Maharashtra (9.29%), Bihar (8.58%) and undivided Andhra Pradesh (7.00%).
57.tq: Order the options by the numerical shares from highest to lowest.
57.sec: State-wise population and area ranking  [other exams]

57.s: Which of the following correctly represents the population-share ranking of West Bengal and undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2011?
57.x: West Bengal ranked fourth with 7.55 per cent of India’s population, while undivided Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth with 7.00 per cent.
57.tq: Distinguish adjacent ranks by their exact percentage shares.
57.sec: State-wise population and area ranking  [other exams]

57.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the least populous States and the area ranking of selected States?
o: Sikkim is the least populous State; Rajasthan is the largest State by area and Goa the smallest State.
Mizoram is the least populous State; Goa is the largest State by area.
Nagaland is the least populous State; Sikkim is the largest State by area.
Goa is the least populous State; Rajasthan is the smallest State by area.
57.x: Sikkim, with about 6.08 lakh people, is the least populous State. Rajasthan is the largest State by area and Goa is the smallest State.
57.tq: Combine two independent rankings without confusing population with area.
57.sec: State-wise population and area ranking  [other exams]

57.s: Which of the following statements about Bihar is correct?
o: It ranked third in both population and area in 2011.
It ranked third in population but twelfth in area in 2011.
It ranked twelfth in population but third in area in 2011.
It ranked first in population and first in area in 2011.
57.x: Bihar was third among States in population but ranked twelfth in area. This contrast contributes to its high population density.
57.tq: Test the reversal between population rank and area rank.
57.sec: State-wise population and area ranking  [other exams]

57.s: Which of the following correctly describes residual Andhra Pradesh in the cited 2024–25 profile?
o: 4th in population, 8th largest by area, and 4.09% share
10th in population, 4.09% share, and 8th largest by area with 1,62,970 sq km
8th in population, 10th largest by area, and 7.00% share
10th in population, 8th largest by area, and 9.29% share
57.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh was placed 10th in population, with a 4.09 per cent share, and 8th in area, covering 1,62,970 square kilometres. Some earlier material rounds the share to 4.10 per cent.
57.tq: Check the complete multi-part profile instead of one isolated rank.
57.sec: State-wise population and area ranking  [other exams]

57.s: Which of the following regions is associated with very high population density because of fertile alluvial soils, water availability and intensive agriculture?
o: Remote tribal hills of the North-East
Ganga plain and the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta
Thar desert and the western Himalayan slopes
57.x: The Ganga plain and the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta are among the densely populated regions of the world. Fertile alluvial soils and water support intensive agriculture there.
57.tq: Link physical characteristics with the resulting population concentration.
57.sec: Regions of high density - Ganga plains, deltas, mining-industrial districts  [other exams]

57.s: The Godavari–Krishna delta region supports high population density primarily because it:
o: Supports intensive rice farming on fertile deltaic land
Contains only thin and rocky soils
Has an extremely cold climate and rugged relief
57.x: The Godavari–Krishna coastal deltas have fertile alluvial and deltaic land and support intensive rice cultivation, favouring dense settlement.
57.tq: Apply the agriculture–settlement relationship to a regional example.
57.sec: Regions of high density - Ganga plains, deltas, mining-industrial districts  [other exams]

57.s: Why is Dhanbad regarded as the most densely inhabited district of the Chotanagpur Plateau?
o: It is an uninhabited high-altitude valley.
It has no mineral-based economic activity.
Mining industries and industrialisation have attracted population.
Its population is supported mainly by shifting cultivation.
57.x: Dhanbad’s high density is associated with coal mining, industrialisation and related employment. BCCL is based there.
57.tq: Identify the economic factor behind a settlement pattern.
57.sec: Regions of high density - Ganga plains, deltas, mining-industrial districts  [other exams]

57.s: Which of the following pairs correctly indicates the urban population percentages of the two cited urban-industrial clusters?
57.x: Delhi had an urban share of 97.50 per cent and Chandigarh 97.25 per cent in the cited comparison.
57.tq: Compare closely placed percentages without reversing the pair.
57.sec: Regions of high density - Ganga plains, deltas, mining-industrial districts  [other exams]

57.s:
Consider the following pairs of factors and population-density outcomes:
1. Plains and gentle slopes — dense population
2. Himalaya and rugged hills — sparse population
3. River valleys — dense population
4. Thar desert — sparse population
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
57.x: All four pairs are correct. Relief and water availability strongly influence the spatial concentration or dispersal of population.
57.tq: Match each physical factor with its associated density pattern.
57.sec: Factors of uneven distribution - plains, valleys, hills, deserts

57.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Extreme hot or cold climate — sparse population
Thin, rocky soils — relatively dense population
57.x: Thin, rocky soils generally support sparse population because they constrain cultivation. Loamy alluvial soils favour dense settlement.
57.tq: Find the one reversed density relationship.
57.sec: Factors of uneven distribution - plains, valleys, hills, deserts

57.s: Which of the following is an exception to the general association of mountainous terrain with sparse population?
o: Himalayan valleys such as Kashmir and parts of Himachal Pradesh
Remote rocky plateaus without water sources
57.x: Although the Himalayas generally have sparse population, valleys such as Kashmir and parts of Himachal Pradesh have relatively higher density and are important exceptions.
57.tq: Look for the stated geographical exception rather than applying a broad rule mechanically.
57.sec: Factors of uneven distribution - plains, valleys, hills, deserts

57.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly classified as a population-resource region?
o: Deficit region—population pressure on degraded resources
Progressive region—resources are unavailable for development
57.x: Progressive regions are resource-developed regions. Problem regions face population pressure on limited or degraded resources, while deficit regions have resources exceeding their use.
57.tq: Discriminate among closely related classification terms by their defining relationship.
57.sec: Population-resource regions of India

57.s: The physiological density of population is calculated as:
o: Total population divided by net cultivated area
Total population divided by total geographical area
Net cultivated area divided by total population
Agricultural population divided by total geographical area
57.x: Physiological density measures total population in relation to net cultivated area. It indicates the pressure of the total population on cultivated land.
57.tq: Distinguish the denominator from those used in arithmetic and agricultural density.
57.sec: Physiological and agricultural density

57.s:
Which of the following formulae is correctly matched with the type of density?
1. Arithmetic density — Total population / total area
2. Physiological density — Total population / net cultivated area
3. Agricultural density — Agricultural population / net cultivable area
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three formulae are correct. Arithmetic density uses total area, physiological density uses net cultivated area, and agricultural density uses agricultural population and net cultivable area.
57.tq: Verify the numerator and denominator in each formula separately.
57.sec: Physiological and agricultural density

57.s: Which demographic changes would generally increase population density in a region, other factors remaining constant?
57.x: Natality adds to population through natural increase, while immigration adds people from outside the region. Mortality and emigration generally reduce density.
57.tq: Apply the population-change equation to a density scenario.
57.sec: Physiological and agricultural density

57.s:
The Census Town criteria retained for Census 2027 include which of the following?
1. Population of at least 5,000
2. Density of at least 400 persons per sq km
3. At least 75% of male working population in non-farm work
4. Criteria introduced only after 2011
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: The criteria are 5,000 people, density of 400 persons per square kilometre and 75 per cent male non-farm workers. They have remained unchanged since 1981, so statement 4 is false.
57.tq: Use the unchanged-since date to eliminate the false chronology statement.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: Which authority is associated with retaining the existing Census Town criteria for Census 2027?

57.tq: Identify the responsible administrative authority rather than the reviewing ministry.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: The reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh into 28 districts is significant for population-density analysis because it:
o: Removed all differences between district and State density
Changed only the national density figure
Made district boundaries irrelevant to density calculations
Changed the districts at the two extremes of density, including Polavaram and Markapuram in the 2025 reorganisation
57.x: The 2025 reorganisation, including Polavaram and Markapuram, changed the district framework and therefore the observed density extremes in Andhra Pradesh.
57.tq: Connect administrative reorganisation with the statistical comparability of district data.
57.sec: Universal angles

57.s: What is a major criticism of measuring population density on administrative boundaries?
o: It uses cultivated area instead of geographical area in every case.
It completely eliminates the effect of migration.
It measures only agricultural population and excludes urban residents.
It may misclassify peri-urban areas because the boundaries do not correspond to the built-up area.
57.x: Administrative boundaries may include non-built-up rural land or exclude functionally connected built-up areas, causing peri-urban areas to be misclassified. This is a limitation of administrative rather than built-up density.
57.tq: Apply the boundary-versus-built-up-area distinction to an urban fringe.
57.sec: Universal angles

A is false but R is true

ignored all forms of contraception and health infrastructure
rejected voluntary choice in favour of informed consent
focused narrowly on sterilisation and suffered from distrust created by Emergency-era coercion
